title: Transgender Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (institutional advanced clinical and scholarly fellowship; public programme page does not state that this is a separately ACGME-accredited specialty programme)-aligned independent study
prerequisites: Physician-level knowledge after internal medicine residency and endocrinology fellowship; BWH lists prior completion of ACGME-accredited U.S. internal medicine and endocrinology training, with possible case-by-case exceptions. This is programme-specific application information, not course admission or a legal eligibility ruling.
Working knowledge of reproductive endocrinology, endocrine physiology, pharmacology, primary care, shared decision-making and evidence appraisal.
This independent self-study course is not an alternative pathway into a fellowship and has no admissions, supervision or clinical credentialing function.
objectives: Explain the publicly described BWH training scope and distinguish it from official accreditation, board blueprints and this independent curriculum.
Reason through individualized TGD endocrine care topics, relevant evidence and uncertainty without issuing patient-specific advice.
Map ABIM endocrine blueprint coverage precisely and identify the limited exam overlap.
Apply affirming communication, fertility/contraception counseling, safety monitoring concepts, organ-informed prevention, team referral and privacy principles.
Critically appraise current guidelines and communicate when law, clinical evidence or board status requires authoritative confirmation.

units.title: Language, identity, access and affirming clinical systems
objectives: Distinguish sex assigned at birth, gender identity, gender expression and sexual orientation without treating any one as a proxy for another.
Conduct a respectful, relevant history using the patient’s names, pronouns, anatomy and goals, and repair an error without making the patient responsible for teaching the clinician.
Identify clinic-workflow, privacy, access, stigma and intersectionality barriers and propose a measurable improvement.
topics: Terminology and culturally situated identities; inclusive registration and documentation; confidential histories; trauma-informed examination; stigma, access and equity; quality-improvement measures.
boardDomains: ABIM endocrine blueprint: health equity content; general internal medicine context (not separately weighted transgender domain).
units.casePractice: Analyze one pseudonymized qualitative family case from the open case study; identify system barriers and avoid treating narrative themes as prevalence estimates.
units.assessment: Submit a 1-page clinic-workflow redesign and a 5-item communication checklist. Rubric: respect/privacy 30%; clinical relevance 25%; feasibility 25%; measures/equity 20%.

units.title: Assessment, shared decisions and informed consent in adult care
objectives: Elicit a person’s desired outcomes and prior care without imposing a uniform transition narrative or requiring a mental-health referral as a universal adult prerequisite.
Explain the distinction among gender identity, a diagnosis used for a specific purpose, treatment indication, and legal/insurance codes.
Use shared decision-making to document benefits, material uncertainties, alternatives, fertility and follow-up.
topics: Clinical assessment; decisional capacity and consent; psychosocial supports and comorbidities without gatekeeping; goals and individualized care plans; documentation and privacy; evidence certainty.
boardDomains: ABIM: Female Reproduction and Male Reproduction (each 7% broad domain; sexual differentiation subsection <2% each); health-equity integration.
units.casePractice: Compare the guideline-derived case-discussion resource with an adult fictional vignette; list missing information before proposing any care.
units.assessment: Write a shared-decision note template. Rubric: elicitation 25%; informed consent/uncertainty 30%; fertility and safety 25%; respectful documentation 20%.

units.title: Puberty, adolescent pathways and boundaries of this adult subspecialty
objectives: Differentiate prepubertal care, puberty-related evaluation and adult hormone care; do not extrapolate adult protocols or board eligibility to pediatric care.
Summarize guideline-described multidisciplinary roles and developmental/contextual assessment while labeling areas where guidelines and local requirements differ.
Identify current jurisdictional consent, safeguarding, confidentiality and service-access questions that require local legal and clinical review.
topics: Development and puberty; multidisciplinary care; adolescent assent/consent and guardian rules; fertility preservation; mental-health support; current local law and referral; avoid universal eligibility claims.
boardDomains: ABIM Endocrinology blueprint: general pediatrics with emphasis on adolescent medicine; Female/Male Reproduction.
units.casePractice: Use an instructional youth case resource to produce a decision map separating clinical questions from jurisdiction-specific questions; do not issue legal conclusions.
units.assessment: Annotated pathway map. Rubric: age distinctions 30%; multidisciplinary roles 25%; uncertainty/legal flags 25%; appropriate referral 20%.

units.title: Endocrine physiology, treatment goals and hormone measurement
objectives: Explain hypothalamic-pituitary-gonadal physiology and feedback relevant to sex-steroid therapy.
Interpret hormone results in context of formulation, timing, anatomy, co-medications, laboratory methods and the patient’s individualized goals.
Describe why a level alone neither defines identity nor proves clinical benefit or harm.
topics: HPG axis; pharmacokinetics and assays; endogenous suppression; reference intervals and limitations; target-setting as individualized; medication reconciliation.
boardDomains: ABIM: Female Reproduction and Male Reproduction (7% each); Hypogonadism within Male Reproduction.
units.casePractice: A fictional lab-interpretation worksheet asks learners to identify absent sampling-time/formulation data before interpreting levels.
units.assessment: Short answer (4 lab vignettes). Rubric: assay/timing 35%; physiology 30%; uncertainty 20%; safe next question 15%.

units.title: Feminizing hormone regimens, safety and monitoring
objectives: Compare common estradiol routes and androgen-lowering options by pharmacology, risks, preference, access and evidence rather than by a one-size dose.
Identify thromboembolic, cardiovascular, medication-interaction and antiandrogen safety questions for clinician review.
Explain why expected effects, timelines, reversibility, non-reversible changes and uncertain add-on benefits must be discussed before treatment.
topics: Estradiol preparations; antiandrogens and monitoring; VTE risk assessment; spironolactone-related potassium/renal monitoring when used; expected effects; progesterone evidence/uncertainty; follow-up. No prescribing instructions.
boardDomains: ABIM: Female Reproduction / sexual differentiation (<2% of exam); Male Reproduction / sexual differentiation (<2%).
units.casePractice: Use an instructional case on estrogen/fertility goals; build a risk-question list without selecting a dose.
units.assessment: One-page comparative reasoning memo. Rubric: pharmacology 25%; risk/monitoring 30%; patient priorities 25%; evidence qualifiers 20%.

units.title: Masculinizing hormone therapy and monitoring
objectives: Describe major testosterone formulations and the interpretation of formulation-timed measurements.
Recognize erythrocytosis, acne/androgenic alopecia, fertility effects and other adverse-effect considerations that prompt individualized assessment.
Discuss desired partial or nonbinary effects without assuming all patients want maximal masculinization.
topics: Testosterone routes/formulations; individualized outcomes; hematocrit and other monitoring considerations; menstrual suppression and pregnancy possibility; testosterone transfer precautions for topical products.
boardDomains: ABIM: Male Reproduction (7%; hypogonadism 2%); Female Reproduction and general internal medicine context.
units.casePractice: Compare fictional patient goals with a free reproductive-access case; identify fertility and contraception counseling needs.
units.assessment: Construct a monitoring rationale, not a prescription. Rubric: formulation/measurement 25%; safety 30%; goal alignment 25%; pregnancy/fertility 20%.

units.title: Fertility, contraception, sexual health and medication interactions
objectives: Counsel that hormone use does not reliably provide contraception and fertility effects are variable; offer timely fertility-preservation discussion and referral.
Reconcile sexual practices, organs present and pregnancy potential without inference from identity or medication.
Use a current interaction resource with HIV/ART or other co-medications and refer uncertain interactions to a pharmacist/specialist.
topics: Oocyte/sperm preservation and reproductive options; contraception and pregnancy; sexual health; HIV/STI care; organ inventory; interaction checking; confidentiality.
boardDomains: ABIM: Female Reproduction (7%) and Male Reproduction (7%); health equity.
units.casePractice: Discuss one of the PDF’s three constructed cases, with attention to its teaching-case status; review the public lecture case only as its presenter’s educational illustration.
units.assessment: Fertility/contraception counseling plan. Rubric: reproductive facts/uncertainty 30%; inclusive history 25%; interaction/specialist referral 25%; communication 20%.

units.title: Cardiometabolic, bone and general endocrine comorbidity
objectives: Apply ordinary evidence-based prevention and comorbidity assessment while recognizing the evidence limits for TGD-specific long-term risk estimates.
Identify when bone-health, cardiometabolic, diabetes, lipid or blood-pressure evaluation is indicated based on individual context.
Distinguish treatment-specific monitoring from screening dictated by age, anatomy, history and current clinical guidance.
topics: Cardiovascular risk; smoking and VTE; lipids/metabolic health; bone mineral density and duration of low sex steroids; obesity/diabetes; comorbidity and medication safety.
boardDomains: ABIM: Lipids, Obesity, and Nutrition (12%); Diabetes (24%); Calcium and Bone (15%); Female/Male Reproduction.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional comorbidity case to separate baseline population screening from hormone-specific monitoring.
units.assessment: Create a one-page risk matrix. Rubric: evidence 30%; individualized risks 30%; correct distinction 20%; follow-up rationale 20%.

units.title: Cancer prevention and screening by organs, exposure and history
objectives: Use anatomy present, prior surgery, hormone exposure, age, family history and local screening recommendations to construct a screening discussion.
Avoid gender identity as a stand-in for organs or screening eligibility.
Communicate uncertainty where evidence for TGD-specific screening intervals is limited and arrange appropriate preventive referrals.
topics: Breast/chest, cervix, uterus/endometrium, ovaries and prostate considerations as applicable; screening evidence; symptoms vs screening; organ inventory; record confidentiality.
boardDomains: ABIM: Female and Male Reproduction; broad endocrine/primary-care reasoning (no transgender-specific exam weighting).
units.casePractice: Learner annotates a fictional organ-inventory chart; no real image or patient record is used.
units.assessment: Screening rationale note. Rubric: anatomy/history 30%; guideline alignment 30%; uncertainty 20%; respectful language 20%.

units.title: Surgery, voice, perioperative care and interdisciplinary referral
objectives: Describe the range of gender-affirming surgery, voice/communication support and other interventions without implying that any intervention is necessary for identity.
Identify endocrine questions for coordination before and after surgery and the need for the operating team’s procedure-specific guidance.
Separate knowledge of indications/complications from technical competence, procedural authorization or surgical training.
topics: Chest/genital/facial surgeries; fertility; perioperative medication planning by responsible teams; postoperative follow-up; voice care; pelvic-floor and mental-health referral; access and consent.
boardDomains: ABIM: Female/Male Reproduction and internal-medicine comorbidity; no separate surgery-board mapping for this fellowship.
units.casePractice: Use linked guideline sections and an openly posted educational overview only; UCLA labels some surgery videos age-restricted and does not publicly post its top-surgery photos/video, so exclude those gated assets.
units.assessment: Referral/co-management map. Rubric: scope/roles 30%; perioperative coordination 30%; options/autonomy 20%; access/privacy 20%.

units.title: Mental health, trauma-informed care, crisis response and resilience
objectives: Assess mental health concerns and safety as clinically indicated without treating TGD identity as pathology or assuming a universal psychiatric cause.
Use trauma-informed, affirming communication and collaborative referral while preserving the clinician’s role boundaries.
Describe structural stress and protective supports without attributing causality beyond the evidence.
topics: Minority stress/resilience; depression/anxiety/substance use and suicide assessment; trauma-informed settings; crisis pathways; social supports; collaboration with behavioral-health colleagues.
boardDomains: ABIM: health-equity content; relevant internal-medicine and adolescent context, no separate TGD exam percentage.
units.casePractice: Discuss a published pseudonymized case-study narrative only via its public article, respecting its small, limited sample; no case excerpts/images are redistributed.
units.assessment: Case conference reflection and referral map. Rubric: clinical/safety response 30%; nonpathologizing approach 25%; evidence limits 25%; collaborative plan 20%.

units.title: Scholarly inquiry, evidence appraisal, ethics, law and practice improvement
objectives: Critically appraise the design, population, limitations and date of clinical guidance and transgender-health evidence.
Design a modest scholarly/QI question and measurement plan with privacy safeguards and community partnership.
Verify rapidly changing policy, board and clinical information from authoritative sources before real-world use.
topics: Guideline comparison; shared decision-making under uncertainty; privacy/HIPAA limits; QI and research distinctions; stakeholder/community engagement; local law and policy review; evidence update cycle.
boardDomains: ABIM: health equity across blueprint; scholarship/QI is program training context, not exam domain.
units.casePractice: Critique source scope and rights for one open case study or case-discussion resource; do not reproduce material without permission.
units.assessment: 2-page evidence brief and small QI proposal. Rubric: source quality/date 30%; method/limitations 25%; privacy/ethics 25%; feasible measure 20%.

assignment.title: Capstone: source-audited fictional endocrine consultation + service improvement brief
assignment.instructions: Use a fictional, non-identifiable case to map goals, clinically relevant history, medication reconciliation, fertility/contraception considerations, monitoring questions, referral/team roles, privacy and current source checks. Do not specify a patient-specific prescription or imply procedural competence. Add a one-page QI metric proposal and distinguish institutional program facts, board domains and guideline statements.

assessment.format: Formative, self-study only; 10 original single-best-answer questions, unit tasks, and a capstone. Not official board questions, standardized, validated, or a passing predictor.
assessment.suggested_completion_standard: Learner-set educational threshold such as 80% on original questions plus satisfactory self-review against assignment rubrics; not an accredited grade or competency attestation.
assessment.practiceQuestions: See practiceQuestions; all questions are original and cited.

unitMap.text: Language, identity, access and affirming clinical systems
coveredTopics: Terminology and culturally situated identities; inclusive registration and documentation; confidential histories; trauma-informed examination; stigma, access and equity; quality-improvement measures.

unitMap.text: Assessment, shared decisions and informed consent in adult care
coveredTopics: Clinical assessment; decisional capacity and consent; psychosocial supports and comorbidities without gatekeeping; goals and individualized care plans; documentation and privacy; evidence certainty.

unitMap.text: Puberty, adolescent pathways and boundaries of this adult subspecialty
coveredTopics: Development and puberty; multidisciplinary care; adolescent assent/consent and guardian rules; fertility preservation; mental-health support; current local law and referral; avoid universal eligibility claims.

unitMap.text: Endocrine physiology, treatment goals and hormone measurement
coveredTopics: HPG axis; pharmacokinetics and assays; endogenous suppression; reference intervals and limitations; target-setting as individualized; medication reconciliation.

unitMap.text: Feminizing hormone regimens, safety and monitoring
coveredTopics: Estradiol preparations; antiandrogens and monitoring; VTE risk assessment; spironolactone-related potassium/renal monitoring when used; expected effects; progesterone evidence/uncertainty; follow-up. No prescribing instructions.

unitMap.text: Masculinizing hormone therapy and monitoring
coveredTopics: Testosterone routes/formulations; individualized outcomes; hematocrit and other monitoring considerations; menstrual suppression and pregnancy possibility; testosterone transfer precautions for topical products.

unitMap.text: Fertility, contraception, sexual health and medication interactions
coveredTopics: Oocyte/sperm preservation and reproductive options; contraception and pregnancy; sexual health; HIV/STI care; organ inventory; interaction checking; confidentiality.

unitMap.text: Cardiometabolic, bone and general endocrine comorbidity
coveredTopics: Cardiovascular risk; smoking and VTE; lipids/metabolic health; bone mineral density and duration of low sex steroids; obesity/diabetes; comorbidity and medication safety.

unitMap.text: Cancer prevention and screening by organs, exposure and history
coveredTopics: Breast/chest, cervix, uterus/endometrium, ovaries and prostate considerations as applicable; screening evidence; symptoms vs screening; organ inventory; record confidentiality.

unitMap.text: Surgery, voice, perioperative care and interdisciplinary referral
coveredTopics: Chest/genital/facial surgeries; fertility; perioperative medication planning by responsible teams; postoperative follow-up; voice care; pelvic-floor and mental-health referral; access and consent.

unitMap.text: Mental health, trauma-informed care, crisis response and resilience
coveredTopics: Minority stress/resilience; depression/anxiety/substance use and suicide assessment; trauma-informed settings; crisis pathways; social supports; collaboration with behavioral-health colleagues.

unitMap.text: Scholarly inquiry, evidence appraisal, ethics, law and practice improvement
coveredTopics: Guideline comparison; shared decision-making under uncertainty; privacy/HIPAA limits; QI and research distinctions; stakeholder/community engagement; local law and policy review; evidence update cycle.

topicGaps: The observed accessible free recording ledger totals 13.761388889 hours (specialty-specific 11.474166667; common-foundation 2.287222222); the 36.000-hour video floor remains short by 22.238611111 hours. No planned target minutes, authored scripts, unknown-duration item, gated item, or duplicate may be added to this count.

The new free recordings broaden adult assessment, youth boundaries, hormone/lab context, fertility, HIV/ART interaction questions, preventive care, surgery/voice referral literacy, behavioural-health roles, access and clinic systems. Existing programme gaps remain: no public BWH itemized didactic syllabus, exact clinical hours, case volume, case mix, milestones, or fellowship lecture set was found; free recordings are scattered, dated, and uneven rather than a coherent 36-hour curriculum.

Several key free recordings are older (UCLA Gender Health series largely 2018–2019; UCSF guideline chapters dated 2016; Endocrine Society guideline 2017; SOC-8 2022). Verify current clinical guidance, product labeling, local law, age-specific consent and access rules before any practice. The UCLA facial-feminization video was excluded because its public watch page identified an age restriction. Some other linked webinar/media candidates remain unknown-duration or gated and uncounted.

Adult and youth assessment, reproductive goals, regimen-specific drug interactions, long-term cardiometabolic/bone/cancer outcomes, organ-specific screening intervals, surgery/perioperative coordination and rapidly changing policy require current primary-source appraisal and supervised clinical experience. Public videos do not establish fellowship curriculum, accreditation, board eligibility or competence.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (institutional advanced clinical and scholarly fellowship; public programme page does not state that this is a separately ACGME-accredited specialty programme)
boardNames: American Board of Internal Medicine (ABIM) — Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism Certification Examination (related prerequisite specialty only; not a Transgender Medicine board examination)
medical.boardStatus: No separate transgender-medicine board examination or ABMS/ABIM certification pathway was identified as of 2026-10-07. ABIM has an Endocrinology, Diabetes, and Metabolism examination. In its January 2026 blueprint, Female Reproduction and Male Reproduction are each 7% of the exam; “sexual differentiation” including gender dysphoria is listed at <2% within each respective category. These are endocrinology exam domains, not a transgender medicine exam or complete fellowship blueprint.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: The BWH page describes applicants as having completed internal medicine residency followed by subspecialty endocrinology training in an ACGME-accredited U.S. programme, subject to case-by-case exceptions, and lists application/visa requirements. This self-study course grants no board eligibility. Only ABIM and relevant authorities determine certification eligibility. No claim of separate accreditation for this specific transgender medicine fellowship is made.

officialProgrammes.name: BWH Transgender Medicine Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official profile says established 2024; 12 months; weekly supervised clinics; rotations with gender surgeons, voice therapists, pelvic physical therapists, mental-health providers and primary care clinicians; didactics/case presentations/conferences; more than half of time on mentored scholarly projects. This is the publicly described scope, not an itemized syllabus, formal rotation-hour map or case-volume record.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The supplied listing is an official Mass General Brigham GME training-directory entry for the exact BWH programme. The programme profile supports that it is a physician fellowship for endocrinologists and mixes supervised clinical training, interdisciplinary exposure, didactics and scholarly work. It is not described as a combined programme or as a research-only postdoctoral supplement. It is not a generic directory category. No separate transgender medicine board exam is identified. The public page does not state a separate ACGME accreditation status or publish an itemized curriculum/case log; ACGME endocrinology requirements apply to the prerequisite endocrinology fellowship, not automatically to this programme.
sourceCaveats: BWH official page is a programme-description source, not an accreditation or board source. It states a 12-month fellowship, interdisciplinary rotations and scholarly focus but does not expose full curriculum, detailed schedules or clinical volumes.
ACGME endocrinology requirements revised September 3, 2025 describe the prerequisite subspecialty discipline. Do not infer the transgender medicine fellowship itself is ACGME-accredited.
ABIM blueprint checked in January 2026. Gender dysphoria/sexual differentiation is a small subsection (<2% in each of two reproductive categories), not a specialty exam blueprint.
Endocrine Society guideline resource links the 2017 practice guideline; it is not a new guideline edition. The hub was accessed October 2026; cross-check current evidence, policies and law.
UCSF guideline hub is second edition dated 2016 and says revision forthcoming 2026; some interim updates exist. Verify page status at use.
WPATH SOC-8 is 2022 consensus guidance; it is not a board blueprint or a statement of local law.
Rapidly changing federal/state/local law, age-specific service rules, formularies, approvals, and payer policies are not exhaustively researched; verify through current official authorities.
No human clinical review was performed. Clinical content is self-study only; not advice for a real patient.

topicGaps: The observed accessible free recording ledger totals 13.761388889 hours (specialty-specific 11.474166667; common-foundation 2.287222222); the 36.000-hour video floor remains short by 22.238611111 hours. No planned target minutes, authored scripts, unknown-duration item, gated item, or duplicate may be added to this count.

The new free recordings broaden adult assessment, youth boundaries, hormone/lab context, fertility, HIV/ART interaction questions, preventive care, surgery/voice referral literacy, behavioural-health roles, access and clinic systems. Existing programme gaps remain: no public BWH itemized didactic syllabus, exact clinical hours, case volume, case mix, milestones, or fellowship lecture set was found; free recordings are scattered, dated, and uneven rather than a coherent 36-hour curriculum.

Several key free recordings are older (UCLA Gender Health series largely 2018–2019; UCSF guideline chapters dated 2016; Endocrine Society guideline 2017; SOC-8 2022). Verify current clinical guidance, product labeling, local law, age-specific consent and access rules before any practice. The UCLA facial-feminization video was excluded because its public watch page identified an age restriction. Some other linked webinar/media candidates remain unknown-duration or gated and uncounted.

Adult and youth assessment, reproductive goals, regimen-specific drug interactions, long-term cardiometabolic/bone/cancer outcomes, organ-specific screening intervals, surgery/perioperative coordination and rapidly changing policy require current primary-source appraisal and supervised clinical experience. Public videos do not establish fellowship curriculum, accreditation, board eligibility or competence.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult asks to discuss gender-affirming hormone therapy and describes a clear treatment goal. Which next step best reflects an individualized endocrine consultation?

options.text: Require a mental-health letter for every adult before discussing treatment.
Elicit goals, relevant history and medications; discuss expected effects, uncertainty, risks, fertility and follow-up using shared decision-making.
Infer desired treatment from gender identity and start a standard regimen.
Defer discussion until the patient has completed a social transition.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Adult assessment should be goal-directed and shared, include health context and informed counseling, and avoid imposing a uniform pathway. Mental-health collaboration may be useful but is not a universal adult prerequisite in the BWH lecture’s description of adult care. Individual clinical standards/local law still apply.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient beginning hormones says future genetic parenthood matters to them. What is the best counseling action before a treatment decision?

options.text: Promise fertility will return after stopping hormones.
Explain that fertility effects may occur and are not reliably reversible or predictable; discuss preservation options and referral before treatment.
State that hormone therapy is contraception.
Avoid fertility discussion unless the patient is married.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guidance recommends counseling on fertility preservation before hormone treatment; effects vary, and hormone therapy does not reliably prevent pregnancy. Avoid promises about future fertility.

practiceQuestions.stem: A transmasculine patient taking testosterone reports sexual activity that could result in pregnancy and asks whether testosterone alone prevents conception. Which response is best?

options.text: Testosterone is a reliable contraceptive once menses stop.
Amenorrhea does not establish infertility; discuss contraception and pregnancy potential based on organs and sexual practices.
Pregnancy is impossible while testosterone is prescribed.
Only gender identity determines whether pregnancy counseling is needed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Testosterone may suppress bleeding but is not reliable contraception. Pregnancy counseling follows organs, exposure and patient goals, not identity labels.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinician receives an estradiol result but has no information about route, last administration or sampling time. What is the most defensible interpretation?

options.text: The value alone proves the regimen is appropriate.
The value alone establishes the patient’s gender identity.
Interpretation is limited; clarify formulation, timing, goals, clinical context and assay before making a clinical judgment.
Discard hormone testing for all patients.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Hormone results depend on formulation/timing and clinical/laboratory context. A number cannot establish identity or independently define benefit or harm.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient using an antiandrogen asks what safety monitoring is relevant. Which answer is most appropriate for a learner?

options.text: Monitoring is never needed because the drug is used for gender-affirming care.
Monitoring is individualized to the specific agent, comorbidities and current clinical guidance; for spironolactone, potassium and renal function are pertinent safety considerations.
Only estradiol is monitored, regardless of medication.
Stop all other medicines before starting.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Monitoring depends on medication and patient factors; spironolactone can affect potassium and kidney function. This is a learning principle, not a patient-specific order.

practiceQuestions.stem: A person uses a name/pronouns that differ from the legal name in a record. Which clinic practice best balances affirming care and privacy?

options.text: Display the legal name on every screen to avoid any inconsistency.
Ask what name/pronouns to use and how/where they can safely appear; collect legally required data discreetly and restrict disclosure appropriately.
Ask the patient to explain the discrepancy at each visit.
Avoid documenting any name.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Respectful systems use affirmed name/pronouns and protect confidential information while meeting necessary record requirements. HIPAA limits/safeguards apply to covered entities; local privacy policies matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult wants partial physical changes and does not want a binary endpoint. What is the best clinical framing?

options.text: Explain that all patients should seek full masculinization or feminization.
Clarify desired effects, possible limits and time course, and build an individualized plan; do not assume treatment goals from identity.
Decline care because only binary identities qualify.
Promise precise control over each physical effect.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Care should align with the individual’s goals and explain that effects may not be individually selectable or fully predictable; SOC-8 includes nonbinary people.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which approach best supports preventive screening for a patient whose gender identity differs from their sex assigned at birth?

options.text: Use identity labels alone to determine which organs are present.
Use an individualized, respectful organ and surgical history plus age, exposures, family history and current screening guidance.
Stop all screening after hormone initiation.
Apply every screening test to every patient regardless of anatomy.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Screening is guided by relevant organs, exposures, age, history and current recommendations. Identity is not a reliable proxy for anatomy.

practiceQuestions.stem: A 16-year-old requests treatment at an adult-focused endocrine service. What is the best first educational response?

options.text: Apply adult criteria and assume the adult clinician can provide all pediatric services.
Recognize this requires age-specific, multidisciplinary clinical assessment and a current review of consent, confidentiality and local law; arrange an appropriate qualified pathway.
Assume all jurisdictions have identical rules.
Treat gender identity itself as a diagnosis requiring psychiatric hospitalization.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Adolescent care is not simply adult care at a younger age; clinical expertise, multidisciplinary roles and local legal requirements must be assessed. The BWH fellowship public description targets trained endocrinologists and does not publish pediatric eligibility details.

practiceQuestions.stem: A team wants to use an image from a public case report in a new teaching video. What should it do?

options.text: Copy any image if it is viewable online.
Confirm the license/permission and consent/privacy conditions; otherwise link to the original and do not reproduce the image or patient record.
Remove the name and assume all rights are cleared.
Assume pseudonymization eliminates copyright.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Public access does not itself grant reuse rights; identifiable health information remains sensitive. Link to original source unless license/permission supports reuse, and do not redistribute records/images without authorization.

unitMap.text: Foundations: anatomy, physiology, genetics and risk
coveredTopics: Map cervical endocrine anatomy, embryology, vascular and neural relationships
explain hormone physiology
recognize hereditary syndromes (MEN1/2, CDC73, RET, familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, SDHx) and indications for genetics/counseling.

unitMap.text: Thyroid nodule triage, ultrasound and cytology
coveredTopics: Integrate TSH, sonographic risk, size, cervical nodal survey, Bethesda cytology and selective FNA
frame shared decisions without using cytology as histology.

unitMap.text: Benign thyroid disease, goiter and thyrotoxicosis
coveredTopics: Compare observation, medical therapy, ablation and surgery for benign nodules/goiter/Graves
identify compressive symptoms, substernal extension, and perioperative endocrine optimization.

unitMap.text: Differentiated thyroid carcinoma and extent of surgery
coveredTopics: Stage and risk-stratify adult DTC
distinguish lobectomy/total thyroidectomy decisions, therapeutic vs prophylactic nodal surgery, active surveillance, RFA, and evolving 2025 ATA recommendations.

unitMap.text: Medullary, anaplastic, poorly differentiated and uncommon thyroid cancers
coveredTopics: Recognize subtype-specific staging, RET/MEN2 evaluation, airway threat, molecularly informed multidisciplinary care, palliation and limits of resectability.

unitMap.text: Primary hyperparathyroidism and differential diagnosis
coveredTopics: Confirm biochemical PHPT
separate FHH, secondary/tertiary disease and medication effects
assess renal/skeletal involvement and contemporary Fifth Workshop surgical criteria.

unitMap.text: Parathyroid localization, operative strategies and reoperative disease
coveredTopics: Explain localization as planning (not diagnosis)
compare focused exploration and bilateral exploration
interpret discordance/negative imaging and reoperative risks
discuss intraoperative adjuncts as context-dependent.

unitMap.text: Thyroid/parathyroid operative anatomy, complications and recovery
coveredTopics: Describe safe operative objectives, laryngeal nerve/voice assessment, calcium/hypoparathyroidism, hematoma/airway response, hypocalcemia prevention and follow-up. This is cognitive teaching, not procedural training.

unitMap.text: Adrenal incidentaloma and functional adrenal disease
coveredTopics: Apply contemporary dedicated imaging and hormonal evaluation to incidentalomas
distinguish cortisol autonomy, aldosteronism, pheochromocytoma and malignancy
discuss surgical indications in multidisciplinary context.

unitMap.text: Pheochromocytoma, paraganglioma and adrenalectomy planning
coveredTopics: Use appropriate biochemical tests and pre-analytic interpretation
identify hereditary risk
outline multidisciplinary preparation and approach selection consistent with current guidelines.

unitMap.text: MEN, hereditary endocrine neoplasia and endocrine NETs
coveredTopics: Integrate syndromic differential, genetic counseling, family implications and multidisciplinary care
distinguish thyroid/parathyroid/adrenal and gastroenteropancreatic NET content
identify where endocrine-surgery board blueprint ends.

unitMap.text: Evidence appraisal, outcomes, ethics and transition to practice
coveredTopics: Critically appraise guideline strength, volume/outcome evidence, bias, access disparities and referral/credential boundaries
synthesize a board-domain mapping and quality improvement question.

topicGaps: Thyroid nodule sonographic pattern, FNA thresholds, Bethesda/molecular testing and benign nodule/goiter/Graves options lack runtime-verified long-form lecture coverage in this ledger.

Adult differentiated thyroid cancer: full 2025 ATA guideline recommendations, risk stratification, nodal compartments, treatment de-escalation and longitudinal surveillance require more primary-source teaching and review; the public DTC guideline recording candidate was unavailable at this check.

Medullary carcinoma, RET/MEN2, pediatric versus adult scope, anaplastic/poorly differentiated/rare histology, airway goals and multidisciplinary systemic therapy remain sparsely represented by counted runtime.

Biochemical PHPT evaluation, FHH/medication/secondary causes, Fifth Workshop criteria, localization as planning, reoperation and postoperative risk remain underrepresented despite the added reoperative cases recording.

Adrenal incidentaloma characterization, cortisol autonomy, primary aldosteronism, PPGL evaluation, hereditary risk, preparation and adrenalectomy principles have no counted specialty lecture coverage.
Pancreatic/GI neuroendocrine tumors, MEN/SDHx/CDC73/RET syndromes, outcomes/quality, equity and referral boundaries need additional specialty-specific instruction.

Board mapping remains limited: ABS/ABOHNS ACTPS FPD addresses adult complex thyroid/parathyroid only; AAES broader adrenal and GEP-NET curriculum domains are not a separate endocrine-surgery board blueprint.
Verified accessible free external lecture runtime remains below the 36-hour floor; scripted episodes are planned teaching inputs, not recorded video and not counted toward runtime.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Surgery (ABS) – Adult Complex Thyroid and Parathyroid Surgery (ACTPS) Focused Practice Designation examination (jointly developed with the American Board of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery; not a broad endocrine-surgery subspecialty board)
American Board of Surgery – General Surgery certification is the underlying certification for general surgeons; this curriculum does not grant or confer it
American Board of Otolaryngology–Head and Neck Surgery (ABOHNS) – underlying otolaryngology certification for eligible ENT surgeons; no separate general endocrine-surgery board identified
medical.boardStatus: No single US board certifies a broad Endocrine Surgery subspecialty. ABS ACTPS FPD is an exam/Focused Practice Designation limited to adult complex thyroid and parathyroid surgery and is not a new board subspecialty certificate. ABS/ABOHNS co-developed its blueprint. ABS lists existing board certification, case/fellowship, license, participation and practice eligibility conditions. Verify candidate-specific current rules directly with ABS/ABOHNS. The AAES accredits comprehensive clinical fellowship programs; it does not issue an endocrine-surgery board certificate. AHNS program accreditation is training-program status, not a separate board credential. No separate ABS/ABOHNS exam is identified for adrenal, pancreatic/GI NET or whole-field endocrine surgery. Current pages checked 2026-10-07.

officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Distinct one-year, one-position clinical fellowship accredited by the American Head and Neck Society (AHNS), with eligibility after otolaryngology or general surgical residency. Focuses on thyroid/parathyroid, adult and pediatric exposure, supervised clinical practice, pathology/cytology, interventional radiology and endocrinology rotations. medical.programmeSourceScope: Discovery starts with the supplied MGB official directory and adds verified Johns Hopkins and Massachusetts Eye and Ear (MGB) official/AHNS/AAES listings. These are distinct clinical programme variants: BWH/MGH comprehensive AAES-accredited integrated programme; Johns Hopkins integrated programme listed by both AAES and AHNS, counted once; MEE one-year AHNS-accredited thyroid/parathyroid-focused fellowship with adult and pediatric exposure. No generic directory category or research-only/non-physician appointment is represented as a clinical fellowship. Do not merge MEE thyroid/parathyroid-only scope with broader comprehensive adrenal/NET curriculum. Institutional programme pages are self-descriptions, not an ACGME curriculum or external quality audit.
sourceCaveats: The packet supplemental-discovery.json and existing MED-X086 program/evidence artifacts were absent at the specified paths; the supplied exact source packet alone was present. No prior per-specialty artifacts were overwritten.

Public institutional pages establish programme self-descriptions, not Accreditation Council for Graduate Medical Education (ACGME) accreditation. No separate ACGME endocrine-surgery fellowship requirement or dedicated broad endocrine-surgery board was located in this scoped check. AAES accreditation is programme accreditation, not board certification.

Johns Hopkins appears in both AAES and AHNS directories. Its official page and AHNS listing describe a single integrated one-year program; no duplicate count. MEE is a separate AHNS-accredited thyroid/parathyroid fellowship, distinct from the BWH/MGH AAES-accredited combined fellowship.

The ABS FPD exam applies only to adult complex thyroid/parathyroid practice and has eligibility rules. It is not certification in adrenal or comprehensive endocrine surgery. Exam eligibility must be verified with ABS/ABOHNS for an individual.

No human clinical review performed. Curriculum must be clinically reviewed and refreshed before high-stakes use. The dated 2014 PPGL, 2016 workflow and 2008 PHPT papers are explicitly paired with newer sources where found.

Video time is observed runtime, not all of it pure didactic time; count includes only unique linked public full video items, not non-clinical explanation or unverified chapters. No planned original videos are counted.

practiceQuestions.stem: An asymptomatic patient has a unilateral homogeneous adrenal mass with unenhanced CT attenuation of 7 HU. Under the 2023 ESE guideline, which statement is best?

options.text: This imaging phenotype is benign and needs no additional imaging, independent of size.
The lesion must be removed because every mass over 2 cm is malignant.
HU is interpretable only after contrast administration.
Biopsy is required before hormone tests.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline says homogeneous lesions with unenhanced HU ≤10 are benign and require no further imaging independent of size. Confirm the stated imaging conditions; it does not obviate appropriate clinical/hormonal assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with an adrenal incidentaloma has a suspicious phenotype and evaluation raises concern for pheochromocytoma. Which is the appropriate initial biochemical test class?

options.text: Plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines.
Serum calcitonin alone.
Needle biopsy before lab evaluation.
No testing unless symptoms are episodic.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Endocrine Society guidance recommends plasma free or urinary fractionated metanephrines for initial PPGL biochemical testing and attention to pre-analytic factors.

practiceQuestions.stem: A known functional pheochromocytoma is being considered for resection. Which preparation principle is supported by Endocrine Society guidance?

options.text: Preoperative blockade is recommended to prevent perioperative cardiovascular complications.
Start beta blockade alone before any other evaluation.
Proceed directly to operation without endocrine preparation.
Routine biopsy is the first step.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends preoperative blockade for functional PPGL, with alpha-adrenergic receptor blockers as first choice; specific care requires specialist management and is not prescribed here.

practiceQuestions.stem: In PHPT, what is the role of parathyroid localization imaging?

options.text: It localizes suspected abnormal tissue for operative planning after biochemical diagnosis and decision for surgery.
A positive scan establishes the biochemical diagnosis.
Negative localization rules out PHPT.
Imaging is required before serum calcium and PTH.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Localization imaging assists preoperative planning and does not establish PHPT diagnosis or independently determine the surgical indication.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which patient characteristic is one of the 2022 Fifth International Workshop thresholds for considering parathyroidectomy in asymptomatic PHPT?

options.text: Age under 50 years.
Any thyroid nodule on ultrasound.
A positive localization scan alone.
Fatigue alone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Age under 50 is one listed criterion; other criteria include serum calcium, skeletal, renal and urinary findings. Use the full guideline and clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has persistent hypercalcemia with elevated/inappropriately normal PTH and low urine calcium. Which key differential must be considered before surgery?

options.text: Familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia.
PTH-independent malignancy-associated hypercalcemia as the only possibility.
Primary hyperaldosteronism.
Adrenal cortical carcinoma.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FHH can mimic PHPT and parathyroidectomy usually does not correct the inherited calcium-sensing phenotype; urinary measures are not infallible and require clinical/genetic context.

practiceQuestions.stem: For an adult with thyroid nodule, what is a core initial evaluation element?

options.text: Serum TSH plus dedicated thyroid/neck ultrasound, with FNA selected by risk and size criteria.
Immediate total thyroidectomy for every nodule.
A normal TSH excludes malignancy.
Routine prophylactic lateral neck dissection.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Current nodule assessment integrates biochemical context, ultrasound risk and cytology when indicated; a single test does not rule out cancer. The 2016 workflow paper is older and should be paired with current ATA guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: Why distinguish therapeutic from prophylactic central neck dissection in thyroid cancer teaching?

options.text: Because evidence of clinically involved nodes and the clinical context inform compartmental surgical planning; prophylactic dissection is not automatically indicated in every cN0 case.
They are identical procedures with no indication differences.
Prophylactic lateral dissection is routine for all nodules.
The distinction depends only on serum TSH.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The ABS blueprint explicitly tests central/lateral neck dissection; current DTC guidance supports individualized decisions rather than routine blanket dissection.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes endocrine surgery fellowship credentialing in the United States?

options.text: There is no single separate general endocrine-surgery board certification; ABS ACTPS FPD is a focused designation for adult complex thyroid/parathyroid surgery and requires existing board credentials/eligibility criteria.
AAES fellowship completion automatically confers board certification in all endocrine surgery.
The ACTPS FPD covers adrenal, pancreatic NET and pediatric surgery.
A public fellowship listing guarantees board eligibility.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS describes the ACTPS FPD as recognizing practice not already subspecialty-certified; its scope is adult complex thyroid/parathyroid and its eligibility includes existing ABS continuous certification and practice/fellowship criteria.

practiceQuestions.stem: An educational video page contains an authentic case discussion, but images are hosted by the publisher and license conditions are unclear. What is the lawful default for this course?

options.text: Link to the source only; do not copy/rehost images or patient material unless an explicit applicable license permits it.
Download screenshots because they are de-identified.
Assume public viewing grants redistribution rights.
Reconstruct a synthetic scan and label it a real patient image.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free-to-view does not mean permission to redistribute, and de-identification does not waive copyright or clinical privacy requirements.

boardNames: American Board of Preventive Medicine (ABPM): Public Health and General Preventive Medicine — related board specialty, not the MGB fellowship name
medical.boardStatus: Population health management is a practice focus, not a separate ABMS/ACGME primary specialty or certification exam. The official MGB page describes a physician Population Health Management Fellowship and a distinct short resident elective. The MGB page does not state that this fellowship is an ACGME-accredited residency, an ABPM-accredited Preventive Medicine residency, or a programme with a fellowship-specific board exam. ABPM separately certifies Public Health and General Preventive Medicine; ACGME lists it as a Preventive Medicine specialty. An ABPM examination exists for eligible candidates, separate from this MGB fellowship.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABPM eligibility is governed by current pathway-specific requirements, including applicable medical license/degree, clinical and specialty training, and graduate coursework. Do not infer eligibility or certification from this fellowship or this course. The MGB public page describes its audience as board-eligible graduating residents, fellows or physicians.

officialProgrammes.name: Population Health Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: The supplied official directory uses this name; the linked current page titles it Population Health Management Fellowship. It describes a one-to-two-year programme for board-eligible graduating residents/fellows or physicians, about 30% clinical care, remainder operational/programmatic/didactic work and mentorship. The separate resident elective is two to four weeks. Full protected didactics, ACGME status for this fellowship and a fellowship-specific board exam are not stated. It offers an optional Harvard Program in Clinical Effectiveness with a separate application/admission process.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Exact MGB institution variant retained from the packet. The name difference between directory and linked page is noted. The optional Harvard Program in Clinical Effectiveness is not automatic or part of this independent course. This is not an institutional course reconstruction.
sourceCaveats: The MGB directory title and current linked page title differ; both are preserved.
MGB describes a one-to-two-year physician fellowship and distinct two-to-four-week elective; public page does not publish full didactics, explicit fellowship ACGME status, or its own board exam.
ABPM Public Health and General Preventive Medicine is separate from this MGB supplementary fellowship and has its own eligibility and examination pathway.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinic reports a 40% preventive-service completion rate. Unknown status is excluded from its denominator. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: It is an unbiased estimate for every eligible patient.
Interpret only with the denominator and missing-status rule; check differential missingness before comparison.
It proves outreach caused the rate.
It is incidence.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Rates depend on numerator, denominator, exclusions and data quality; differential unknown status can bias comparisons. A dashboard is not causal evidence.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement best describes MSSP ACO accountability?

options.text: Quality, cost and experience for an assigned Medicare fee-for-service population.
Guaranteed shared savings when utilization falls.
Hospital-only quality with no physician participation.
Preventive medicine board certification.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CMS defines ACO accountability for quality, cost and experience for an assigned Medicare FFS population. Shared savings are conditional, not guaranteed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A language-preference subgroup has lower screening completion. What should the team do first?

options.text: Assume preference causes the gap and lower the target.
Validate stratified measures and data, then partner with patients and teams to identify language and workflow barriers.
Send the same reminder to everyone and declare the disparity addressed.
Treat the gap as proof of individual causation.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Validate denominator and data capture; involve affected people to identify barriers and co-design action. A group difference does not prove individual causation.

practiceQuestions.stem: A single clinic sees fewer emergency visits after a care-management programme, with no comparison group. What conclusion is strongest?

options.text: The programme caused the decline.
The decline is compatible with benefit but may reflect secular trends, case mix, coding or regression to the mean.
There was no effect because it was not randomized.
The programme is cost-effective.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Uncontrolled pre/post analysis describes change but cannot confidently attribute it to an intervention. A stronger comparison and design-specific caveats are needed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Before clinicians act on a claims-derived diabetes care-gap flag, which safeguard matters most?

options.text: Treat the flag as confirmed diagnosis.
Validate data freshness, cohort logic and subgroup performance; permit clinical confirmation and correction.
Reduce outreach to high-complexity patients.
Hide provenance to avoid questioning the model.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Data freshness, cohort validity, subgroup performance, provenance and clinical confirmation reduce error and bias. A population flag is not a diagnosis.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the best balanced improvement measurement plan for a discharge follow-up test?

options.text: Only annual total cost.
A defined process measure, patient-centered outcome, and balancing measure with denominator and time.
Only staff satisfaction.
Unstratified call attempts.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A small test needs process and meaningful outcomes plus balancing effects; define numerator, denominator, exclusions and observation period.

practiceQuestions.stem: A clinic automates outreach for an overdue screening. Which principle is safest?

options.text: A registry makes the final decision for an individual.
Use current guidance, verify eligibility and contraindications in individual care, and support informed shared decisions.
Only contact people cheapest to reach.
Assume screening benefits everyone.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Population outreach supports access, but current recommendation, individual context, harms, contraindications and shared choice still matter.

practiceQuestions.stem: A proven intervention has low uptake in a community with different language access and staffing. Best implementation response?

options.text: Abandon core functions immediately.
Assess local barriers with stakeholders, select strategies, document adaptation, and monitor fidelity and outcomes.
Call it noncompliance.
Treat adoption as clinical effectiveness.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Implementation requires determinant and context assessment. Uptake is an implementation outcome, not clinical effectiveness.

practiceQuestions.stem: A county detects a respiratory illness cluster above baseline. What is the appropriate initial population-health approach?

options.text: Assume the source and launch mass action before confirming cases.
Verify signal and case definition, describe person/place/time, assess data quality, and coordinate with public-health authorities.
Use hospital readmission to estimate incidence.
Wait for certainty before any risk communication.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Signal verification and case definition precede description and appropriate coordination; communicate timely information with uncertainty.

practiceQuestions.stem: A leader considers scaling a promising pilot. Which memo best supports a responsible decision?

options.text: One point estimate, no limitations.
Define population, evidence and uncertainty, capacity, cost perspective, equity, safety/balancing measures and scale/stop criteria.
Assume less utilization always means better health.
Budget unobserved savings as certain.

practiceQuestions.rationale: A go/no-go decision weighs evidence, feasibility, cost, equity, safety and continuation criteria; savings are not guaranteed and utilization alone is not health.

medical.trackType: Clinical physician fellowship (two institution-specific offerings; independent educational course)
boardNames: American Board of Obesity Medicine (ABOM) certification examination (separate physician certification; DABOM designation after eligibility and passing exam)
medical.boardStatus: ABOM offers a physician certification examination. ABOM states it continues to position for possible ABMS subspecialty recognition in future; this is not currently an ABMS-recognized subspecialty board certification based on ABOM public status statement. There is no separate ABMS obesity subspecialty examination. The named fellowships do not themselves award ABOM certification. Verify current ABOM eligibility directly.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This course grants no exam eligibility. ABOM fellowship pathway requires active unrestricted US/Canada license, completed US/Canada residency, active ABMS-member-board or osteopathic-equivalent certification, completion of an Obesity Medicine Fellowship Council-recognized obesity fellowship within 36 months of application deadline, director attestation and passing ABOM exam. MGH page states ACGME residency prerequisite; BWH page states accredited IM or FM residency. Neither page alone establishes that its programme is currently recognized by OMFC; candidates must verify directly.

officialProgrammes.name: BWH Obesity Medicine Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes one-year clinical fellowship at Center for Weight Management and Wellness; eligible applicants completed accredited internal medicine or family medicine residency; about 8 sessions/week, 90% outpatient/10% inpatient, optional pediatric obesity, OB/GYN, diabetes, sleep, surgery, behavioral health and dietitian experiences, weekly didactics/journal club/cases/team discussions. Public summary only; not a complete syllabus or evidence of ACGME subspecialty accreditation.

officialProgrammes.name: MGH Subspecialty Fellowship in Obesity Medicine and Nutrition
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes advanced clinical fellowship at OMNI; requires completed ACGME-accredited residency; about 8 sessions/week, 90% outpatient/10% inpatient and similar optional rotations; weekly didactics, journal club, case presentations; manuscript and Endocrinology Grand Rounds presentation required. Public summary only; no claim that MGH and BWH are a combined programme.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Official MGB programme pages establish two institution-specific clinical fellowship offerings, not a combined programme and not a complete public syllabus. They describe overlapping clinic, multidisciplinary, didactic and rotation features. Public pages do not establish board accreditation, guarantee eligibility or disclose all teaching content. The category is an actual physician clinical fellowship, not generic directory label, research-only postdoc or non-physician supplement.
sourceCaveats: Official programme pages were fetched; clinical activity fractions and curriculum descriptions are institutional summaries and may change.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult is concerned that BMI does not reflect overall health. Which response is most appropriate?

options.text: BMI alone fully measures adiposity and health risk
Use BMI as one classification measure alongside history, examination, complications, function and goals
Ignore BMI and all weight history
Diagnose secondary endocrine disease from BMI alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: BMI is a useful measure but not a complete individual health assessment; evaluate context and complications.
practiceQuestions.domain: ABOM A13; NIDDK BMI and assessment context

practiceQuestions.stem: Which set best captures a board-blueprint-aligned initial history?

options.text: Weight trajectory only
Nutrition, weight, eating behavior, activity, sleep, medication, neuropsychiatric and social history
Only current calorie intake and exercise
Only family history

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABOM separately identifies the multidimensional history domains.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient reports pregnancy planning during discussion of weight medication. What is the safest general next step?

options.text: Start any weight-loss drug at a low dose
Avoid treatment discussion
Review current product labeling and specialist guidance; NIDDK cautions against anti-obesity medication during pregnancy or planned pregnancy
Switch to two weight-loss medicines

practiceQuestions.rationale: NIDDK states weight management medicines may harm a fetus and are not advised in pregnancy/planning; specific decisions require current labels and clinician care.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional 14-year-old has severe obesity. Which approach aligns with AAP guidance?

options.text: Apply adult BMI thresholds and arrange immediate operation
Use pediatric growth criteria and offer referral for multidisciplinary surgical evaluation when severe-obesity criteria are met
Defer all treatment until adulthood
Use adult medication thresholds only

practiceQuestions.rationale: AAP KAS 13 recommends offering referral for adolescents 13+ with severe obesity for evaluation at a comprehensive multidisciplinary pediatric surgery center; referral is evaluation, not automatic operation.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement correctly characterizes BWH and MGH programmes?

options.text: One combined programme with one common curriculum
Two separately named clinical fellowships with overlapping public curriculum features
One is a board exam
Both are research-only postdocs

practiceQuestions.rationale: Official MGB pages describe distinct BWH and MGH programmes; do not collapse exact institutional names or infer a common syllabus.
practiceQuestions.domain: BWH and MGH official programme pages

practiceQuestions.stem: What credential can completion of an obesity medicine fellowship itself confer?

options.text: ABMS subspecialty certification automatically
ABOM Diplomate status automatically
Neither; ABOM has a separate certification examination with eligibility requirements
State medical license

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABOM requires credentials plus a recognized fellowship pathway and exam; fellowship alone is not certification or licensure.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which published ABOM blueprint distribution is correct?

options.text: Evaluation 60%, treatment 37%, professionalism 3%
Evaluation 37%, treatment 60%, professionalism 3%
All domains equally weighted
Treatment 100%

practiceQuestions.rationale: The current linked ABOM outline lists A 37%, B 60%, C 3%; weights approximate.

practiceQuestions.stem: An adult asks which treatment to choose. What is the best general principle?

options.text: Offer the same diet to everyone
Match evidence-based options to goals, comorbidities, risks, access and preferences; include longitudinal care
Use surgery solely for painful symptoms
Medication replaces nutrition and activity support

practiceQuestions.rationale: NIDDK presents multiple modalities; individualized selection and long-term support are needed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A learner uses a public clinical trial registry to make a case discussion. What is an appropriate data-use rule?

options.text: Download identifiable patient records
Use public study-level summaries and do not copy/rehost patient-level records or images
Assume all trial content is public domain
Infer unreported clinical outcomes

practiceQuestions.rationale: Registry records support evidence appraisal but do not grant rights to private records or images; avoid invented data.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description of the MGH fellowship public page is supported?

options.text: Guaranteed ABOM exam pass
Public description includes outpatient/inpatient sessions, possible rotations, weekly didactics and scholarly requirement
Complete formal curriculum is freely published
Accredited obesity subspecialty board

practiceQuestions.rationale: The programme page gives selected public elements and manuscript/Grand Rounds requirement; it is not a complete syllabus or board award.

practiceQuestions.stem: mPAP 27, PAWP 12, CO 5 L/min. What pattern?

options.text: Precapillary PH
Isolated postcapillary PH
Combined post-/precapillary PH
No PH

practiceQuestions.rationale: PVR=(27−12)/5=3 WU. Meets precapillary hemodynamic definition, but not enough alone to diagnose WHO group 1 PAH.

practiceQuestions.stem: mPAP 31, PAWP 19, PVR 1.8 WU. Best label?

options.text: Precapillary PH
Isolated postcapillary PH
Combined post-/precapillary PH
Exercise PH

practiceQuestions.rationale: mPAP >20, PAWP >15 and PVR ≤2 define isolated postcapillary PH.

practiceQuestions.stem: Echo suggests high pulmonary pressure in a patient with dyspnea. What confirms PH hemodynamically?

options.text: Repeat echo
Quality-assessed RHC
CT alone
Six-minute walk

practiceQuestions.rationale: Echo estimates probability; right-heart catheterization measures defining hemodynamics in clinical context.

practiceQuestions.stem: Suspected PH with mismatched V/Q defects. Best next conceptual step?

options.text: Label idiopathic PAH
Expert CTEPH/CTEPD evaluation
Begin PAH medication without confirmation
Rule out CTEPH if routine CT is unrevealing

practiceQuestions.rationale: Mismatched perfusion defects warrant chronic thromboembolic evaluation; anatomy and treatment require expert assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which defines exercise PH in the 2022 ESC/ERS guideline?

options.text: Peak mPAP >20 alone
mPAP/CO slope >3 mmHg/L/min
PAWP >15 at any exercise
PVR >2 alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guideline exercise PH uses mPAP/CO slope >3 mmHg/L/min between rest and exercise.

practiceQuestions.stem: Who may undergo acute vasoreactivity testing to find CCB responders?

options.text: All PH groups
Selected idiopathic, heritable or drug-associated PAH at expert RHC
All group 2 PH
All CTEPH

practiceQuestions.rationale: Testing is for selected PAH; positive response includes mPAP fall ≥10 to ≤40 mmHg with CO unchanged or increased. Not a blanket test.

practiceQuestions.stem: SSc, very low DLCO, hypoxemia, septal lines; edema after vasodilator. Best interpretation?

options.text: Proves idiopathic PAH
Consider PVOD/PCH and urgent expert reassessment
Excludes PH
Increase vasodilator without review

practiceQuestions.rationale: Combination raises concern for PVOD/PCH-spectrum disease and drug-associated edema; no single sign proves it.

practiceQuestions.stem: Most defensible Group 3 statement?

options.text: Apply full PAH algorithm to all
Use systemic vasodilators for all
Optimize lung disease/hypoxemia; consider only phenotype- and indication-specific treatment
Treat echo estimate alone

practiceQuestions.rationale: Group 3 management is phenotype-specific; current US label includes inhaled treprostinil in PH-ILD, not all Group 3.

practiceQuestions.stem: Persistent PH with chronic thromboembolic obstruction. Which statement is accurate?

options.text: All are inoperable
Expert team considers PEA, BPA and/or medical therapy
Anticoagulation always resolves chronic disease
Group 1

practiceQuestions.rationale: CTEPH is Group 4; multimodal expert assessment. Labelled riociguat use is indication-specific.

practiceQuestions.stem: mPAP 23, PAWP 9, PVR 1.8 WU. Interpretation?

options.text: Precapillary PH
Postcapillary PH
PH threshold met but neither pre- nor postcapillary profile
Proves PAH

practiceQuestions.rationale: mPAP >20 is PH; PVR ≤2 and PAWP ≤15 do not meet precapillary or postcapillary definitions; consider unclassified pattern/context.
