Explain venous, arterial and lymphatic anatomy, physiology and mechanisms of edema, reflux, obstruction and thrombosis.
Select conceptual diagnostic pathways for chronic venous disease, VTE and lymphedema while stating uncertainty and limits.
Compare evidence and guideline frameworks for conservative and interventional care without producing patient-specific treatment recommendations.
Recognize emergencies, complications and conditions requiring professional assessment or multidisciplinary escalation.
Distinguish public programme description, board blueprint, clinical guidance, and independent educational content.

units.title: Foundations: venous, lymphatic, arterial anatomy and hemodynamics
objectives: Map superficial, deep, pelvic and upper-body venous anatomy plus lymph drainage.
Explain valves, calf-muscle pump, pressure gradients and edema mechanisms.
topics: Anatomy; variants; embryology; genetics; venous return; low-output vs high-output lymph failure.
units.casePractice: Compare a fictional unilateral-swelling vignette against venous, lymphatic, arterial, systemic and mass-effect mechanisms; submit an annotated concept map.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Clinical evaluation and phenotype classification
objectives: Structure a history and examination for swelling, pain, skin change, ulcer, thrombosis and pelvic symptoms.
Apply CEAP, VCSS, Villalta and SVP terminology while stating their limits.
topics: Risk and family history; medication/systemic causes; pulses; skin; ulcer; CEAP 2020; VCSS; Villalta; quality-of-life instruments.
units.casePractice: Classify two fictional cases and justify which missing findings prevent definitive classification.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Venous duplex, physiology and cross-sectional imaging
objectives: Explain venous duplex acquisition logic and interpret reflux/obstruction data in context.
Select among duplex, CTV, MRV, venography, IVUS and physiologic tests conceptually.
topics: Standing/reverse-Trendelenburg reflux exam; augmentation; reflux thresholds; DUS limitations; APG/PPG; CTV/MRV; IVUS; lymphatic imaging.
units.casePractice: Complete a fictional duplex quality worksheet; distinguish observation, interpretation, uncertainty and escalation.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Chronic superficial venous disease and varicosities
objectives: Differentiate axial reflux, junctional reflux, tributary disease and recurrent varicosities.
Summarize guideline-supported management options without making an individual treatment recommendation.
topics: CEAP C2-C6; reflux mapping; patient-centered selection; compression; thermal/nonthermal ablation; phlebectomy; sclerotherapy; follow-up.
units.casePractice: Evidence matrix: match a fictional presentation to possible options and guideline statements, marking contraindication/uncertainty questions.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Chronic venous hypertension, edema, wounds and ulceration
objectives: Develop a broad differential for lower-limb edema and ulceration.
Relate venous hypertension to skin injury and wound healing; identify arterial assessment needs.
topics: C3-C6; mixed arterial/venous disease; ABI; wound differential; compression rationale and safety caveats; infection; recurrence prevention.
units.casePractice: Construct a fictional differential and source-annotated wound assessment; do not prescribe compression intensity.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: VTE, superficial thrombosis and pulmonary embolism
objectives: Apply pretest-probability logic before testing for DVT/PE.
Summarize anticoagulation phases and recognize treatment tradeoffs and exclusions.
topics: Wells/pretest probability; D-dimer; ultrasound; PE pathways; provoked/unprovoked VTE; DOAC caveats; duration; SVT; filters; PERT/emergency red flags.
units.casePractice: For a fictional suspected DVT, lay out probability-dependent test logic and explain why a positive D-dimer alone cannot establish diagnosis.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Deep venous obstruction, post-thrombotic disease and compression syndromes
objectives: Recognize post-thrombotic syndrome and proximal obstruction patterns.
Compare the goals and limitations of conservative and invasive strategies.
topics: Villalta; iliocaval obstruction; venous claudication; May-Thurner as an anatomic finding requiring clinical context; IVUS; stents/bypass overview; IVC filter retrieval.
units.casePractice: Interpret a fictional pattern of edema, collateral veins and abnormal waveform; list confirmatory information and referral questions.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Pelvic venous disorders and venous compression syndromes
objectives: Use symptom, varix, pathophysiology framework to organize pelvic venous disorders.
Avoid treating radiographic compression alone as disease.
topics: Pelvic pain; vulvar and sciatic varices; renal vein and iliac compression; nutcracker and May-Thurner differentials; pregnancy; multimodality imaging; embolization/stent evidence.
units.casePractice: Create a fictional case conference brief separating symptoms, anatomy, hemodynamics, differential and uncertainty.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Lymphatic biology, lymphedema evaluation and differential
objectives: Distinguish primary and secondary lymphatic dysfunction and high-output edema.
Build a differential and staged evaluation for limb swelling.
topics: ISL staging; limb measurement limitations; venous, cardiac, renal, malignant, medication and infection mimics; lymphoscintigraphy/MRL/ICG context.
units.casePractice: Review a fictional post-cancer swelling vignette; identify venous thrombosis, recurrence and infection that require consideration before attributing to lymphedema.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Lymphedema conservative and surgical care
objectives: Describe components of complete decongestive therapy and the evidence limitations.
Compare conservative care, pneumatic devices and surgical approaches at a conceptual level.
topics: Skin care; exercise; compression; therapist roles; pneumatic compression; lymphatic microsurgery/liposuction; cellulitis; shared decision-making; outcome measures.
units.casePractice: Critique a fictional care proposal for evidence strength, patient goals, safety and need for specialist assessment.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Vascular anomalies, aneurysms and rare venous/lymphatic presentations
objectives: Classify vascular anomalies using current ISSVA terminology.
Recognize presentations requiring multidisciplinary assessment or urgent escalation.
topics: Venous, lymphatic, arteriovenous and combined malformations; congenital variants; aneurysms; tumors; ISSVA; acute limb threat; phlegmasia; compartment syndrome.
units.casePractice: Use a fictional anomaly scenario to distinguish slow-flow vs high-flow questions and identify urgent escalation signals.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

units.title: Therapeutic modalities, complications, ethics and integrated review
objectives: Compare mechanisms and major risk categories across venous treatment modalities.
Integrate the four ABVLM domains while distinguishing knowledge review from procedural competence.
topics: Compression; drugs; sclerotherapy; thermal/nonthermal ablation; embolization; anesthesia; infection control; emergency/complication recognition; informed consent; evidence appraisal.
units.casePractice: Submit a fictional multidisciplinary M&M analysis with contributing factors, guideline citations, limits and a learning plan; never practice procedures from this module.
units.assessment: Formative case worksheet scored for domain accuracy (35%), reasoning and uncertainty (30%), evidence citation (25%), and safety/escalation boundaries (10%).

assignment.title: Fictional case portfolio: swollen limb and venous/lymphatic decision-making
assignment.instructions: Prepare six fictional, source-cited case analyses: suspected acute DVT; chronic venous reflux/ulcer; suspected proximal venous obstruction; post-cancer swelling; pelvic venous symptoms; vascular anomaly. For each, separate observed information from inferences, give a differential, name a defensible supervised diagnostic approach, identify missing information, explain relevant guideline limits, and state urgent escalation questions. Do not copy images or patient records; no procedure practice.
deliverables: Six structured 500-word case analyses with primary-source citations
One one-page mapping of ABVLM exam domains and 2025 published weights
One video/case rights and privacy attestation
One reflection distinguishing course knowledge from clinical competence
assignment.gradingPlan: Formative independent-learning exercise; no clinical sign-off, credential or validated board-passing predictor.

assessment.format: Twelve unit quizzes/case worksheets, a six-case portfolio and ten original formative MCQs.
assessment.passingClaim: No score predicts ABVLM exam success, eligibility, clinical competence, licensure or certification. The question set is not official ABVLM content.
assessment.integrity: All included questions are newly authored; they are not recalled, copied or leaked board items.

boardStatus.status: ABVLM currently publishes a distinct physician certification process, cognitive examination, application pathways and a public examination content outline. This is not an ABMS subspecialty certification claim. No separate ACGME specialty board is claimed.
boardStatus.blueprintScope: The public ABVLM Exam Content Outline effective 2025 totals 100% across: Basic science 21%; Diagnostic evaluation 32%; Knowledge and skills integral to practice 28%; Clinical management 19%. boardStatus.institutionalTrack: The MGH page describes a one-year clinical and research academic fellowship across vascular medicine/surgery, cardiology and interventional radiology, with supervised clinical experience and research. It calls ABVLM exam eligibility an opportunity; it does not establish that this specific fellowship is ACGME-accredited or guarantees ABVLM eligibility. The public page states completed relevant residency/fellowship and its application list asks for ACGME-training documentation; contact programme for applicant criteria.
boardStatus.notBoardEligible: No course completion, video hour, assessment score or case simulation supplies ABVLM pathway eligibility, supervised case counts, venous ultrasound logs, medical licensure, or credentialing.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: ABVLM’s February 2026 candidate handbook lists pathway-specific prerequisites, which include specified ACGME/RCPSC/AOA/other training, medical licensure, board status, CME, ultrasound logs and/or VLM case logs depending on pathway, plus its cognitive exam. Verify the current rules directly with ABVLM. This independent course cannot confer ACGME credit, licensure, eligibility, case-volume credit, procedural competence or certification; it cannot guarantee passing.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This is a true clinical physician fellowship listing, not merely a generic directory category and not research-only: the official MGH programme page describes supervised clinical experience, rotations and required original research. It is also not a combined board programme; breadth across departments is a multidisciplinary rotation model. The page refers broadly to “students with backgrounds in medicine, radiology, or surgery” but elsewhere describes physicians; the exact applicant population and ACGME status are not fully resolved by the public page. Only the one exact listed MGH institutional variant is included. No non-physician supplemental programme or other institutional variant was found/added. No claim of ACGME accreditation is made.
sourceCaveats: Public MGH page confirms an active-described one-year programme, but does not establish this fellowship’s ACGME accreditation; public description uses “students” ambiguously while also requiring relevant prior residency/fellowship and ACGME-training documentation. Contact programme for definitive applicant/credentialing details.

ABVLM publishes a separate cognitive certification exam and pathways; requirements vary and change. Do not call this an ABMS board, ACGME programme or automatic eligibility route. Current ABVLM handbook should be checked directly before application.
The ASH VTE diagnosis webpage says guidelines were reviewed in 2022 and were being monitored pending revision; recheck current recommendations before clinical use.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional adult has new unilateral leg swelling after recent surgery. Before choosing imaging, which conceptual step is most appropriate?

options.text: Assume DVT because surgery is a risk factor
Estimate pretest probability and choose a validated probability-dependent diagnostic pathway
Use a positive D-dimer as diagnostic confirmation
Begin compression and reassess in a month

practiceQuestions.rationale: Pretest probability structures test choice; a risk factor does not establish DVT, and D-dimer alone is not a diagnostic confirmation in high-probability settings. Follow local current pathways and qualified clinical assessment.

practiceQuestions.stem: An otherwise stable fictional patient has suspected DVT and high pretest probability. Which statement is best?

options.text: A positive D-dimer alone confirms DVT
A negative D-dimer alone reliably excludes DVT in every high-probability population
Use imaging-based evaluation according to an evidence-based high-probability pathway; D-dimer alone is not sufficient
Use CEAP class to confirm acute thrombosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASH diagnostic guidance uses pretest probability and imaging strategy; a positive D-dimer alone should not be treated as diagnostic in high-PTP populations.

practiceQuestions.stem: Duplex shows >1 second reversed flow in the common femoral vein. Under SVS/AVF/AVLS guideline definitions, what threshold applies to common femoral, femoral and popliteal reflux?

options.text: >1 second

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline states >1 second for common femoral, femoral and popliteal veins; the >500 ms threshold applies to listed superficial truncal/tibial/deep femoral/perforator veins.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has advanced chronic venous skin change and new thigh fullness. What is the most defensible next reasoning step?

options.text: Assume isolated superficial reflux
Consider evaluation for iliofemoral obstruction as part of a broader duplex/other imaging work-up
Classify the patient as lymphedema without further assessment
Ablate the great saphenous vein because it is always first-line

practiceQuestions.rationale: The 2023 multisociety guideline says CEAP C3-C6 warrants DUS or other imaging to evaluate iliofemoral obstruction; preserve clinical context and outflow.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is an accurate statement about the 2023 ISL lymphedema consensus document?

options.text: It is a definitive legal standard that overrides individual clinical judgment
It synthesizes international practices while acknowledging evidence limitations and need for individualized assessment
It states all limb swelling after cancer treatment is lymphedema
It replaces assessment for DVT and infection

practiceQuestions.rationale: The consensus expressly notes it is not meant to override individual care, acknowledges evidence limitations, and does not make cancer history alone diagnostic.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with limb swelling and prior axillary surgery is assessed for lymphedema. Which consideration is explicitly important?

options.text: Exclude or evaluate other causes such as DVT, malignancy and infection when indicated
Use limb circumference as an infallible standalone diagnostic criterion
Assume MR lymphography is mandatory and definitive
Ignore baseline and contralateral differences

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI PDQ emphasizes differential causes including DVT, malignancy and infection and notes measurement limitations; no single measurement threshold is universally definitive.

practiceQuestions.stem: For a typical adult with objectively confirmed DVT/PE, what broad primary-treatment duration does the ASH 2020 guideline suggest over 6–12 months?

options.text: 1–2 weeks
3–6 months
18–24 months for everyone
Lifelong anticoagulation for every provoked event

practiceQuestions.rationale: ASH suggests a shorter 3–6-month primary treatment course over 6–12 months; after that, the continue/stop secondary prevention decision depends on recurrence and bleeding risks and context.

practiceQuestions.stem: A radiology report notes iliac vein compression in a fictional patient without compatible symptoms or hemodynamic evidence. What conclusion is sound?

options.text: Anatomic compression alone always proves a symptomatic syndrome
The finding needs clinical and hemodynamic correlation; anatomy alone does not establish disease
Immediate stenting is mandatory
This establishes a lymphatic malformation

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABVLM domains and venous guideline evidence require interpretation in clinical context; imaging variation alone is not equivalent to an indication for intervention.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which ABVLM certification statement is accurate as of the checked 2026 public materials?

options.text: There is no separate venous/lymphatic physician exam
ABVLM describes a cognitive exam with distinct pathways and separate prerequisites; completion of this course does not qualify a learner
Any learner with 36 video hours becomes board eligible
ABVLM is identical to the ABMS subspecialty boards

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABVLM publishes an exam blueprint, cognitive exam, application pathways and eligibility requirements. The MGH page mentions eligibility; this self-study course does not establish any pathway prerequisite.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the proper status of a planned 3-hour learning module that has not been recorded and duration-probed?

options.text: Verified free video hours
Observed runtime if its script is complete
Planned production only, not available video and not counted
A playlist duration

practiceQuestions.rationale: Contract policy and lecture evidence rules require accessible existing recordings with observed duration; scripts/plans are never verified media.

practiceQuestions.stem: Persistent exertional symptoms with non-obstructive coronary arteries: safest inference?

options.text: A negative standard stress test excludes coronary cause.
Consider INOCA; a negative conventional test does not always exclude occult coronary cause.
Symptoms are necessarily non-cardiac.
Repeat angiography is always required.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Ongoing symptoms may justify evaluation for an occult coronary mechanism; conventional stress testing can miss it. [CHEST]

practiceQuestions.stem: ACS in a younger patient with few atherosclerotic risks and long smooth coronary narrowing: next thought?

options.text: Consider SCAD in context.
This proves plaque rupture.
OCT is risk-free and mandatory.
Normal first troponin excludes SCAD.

practiceQuestions.rationale: SCAD can present with diffuse stenosis; imaging tools can help but have risks. [SCAD]

practiceQuestions.stem: What does the official MGB page describe?

options.text: A separate ABIM board specialty.
Focused training in women’s CVD including pregnancy, SCAD and microvascular disease.
Replacement for cardiology fellowship.
Independent licensure.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Programme site requires previous cardiology fellowship; ABIM does not list a separate Women’s Heart Health exam. [MGB][ABIM]

practiceQuestions.stem: A prior preeclampsia history years later should be treated as:

options.text: Irrelevant after delivery.
Part of life-course risk history, interpreted with current factors.
Automatic lifelong aspirin indication.
Proof of atherosclerotic disease.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Adverse pregnancy outcome is relevant risk history, not a stand-alone diagnosis or drug mandate. [AHA APO]

practiceQuestions.stem: Pregnancy Heart Team purpose?

options.text: Override patient preference.
Coordinate risk-informed preconception through postpartum care.
Authorize self-study clinical decisions.
Guarantee outcomes.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Guidelines emphasize coordinated multidisciplinary care; local arrangements vary. [ESC]

practiceQuestions.stem: Menopausal hormone therapy and CVD prevention: best framing?

options.text: Universal prevention for all.
Individualize symptom goals and risk; not universal CVD prevention.
All preparations have identical risk.
Risk independent of timing.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AHA statement reviews timing and risk; no blanket preventive indication. [MENO]

practiceQuestions.stem: Can a free-to-view AHA angiographic figure be copied into course slides by default?

options.text: Yes, free access grants reuse.
No; link to source and secure permission or a clear open licence.
Yes, if attributed.
Yes, if de-identified.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Copyright applies; public viewing is not a reuse grant. [SCAD]

practiceQuestions.stem: MGB requires prior cardiology fellowship. This means:

options.text: Self-study substitutes for entry criteria.
Institutional prerequisite, distinct from board policy/accreditation.
Completers qualify for a board exam.
Admission guaranteed.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Institutional admission and board policies differ. [MGB][ABIM]

practiceQuestions.stem: Thoracic aortopathy in pregnancy should prompt a learner to:

options.text: Authorize delivery mode.
Recognize individualized risk and refer to specialist multidisciplinary evaluation.
Assume female risk is lower.
Ignore family history.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Aortopathy and pregnancy require individualized clinical expertise; self-study does not authorize management. [ESC]

practiceQuestions.stem: An observational sex association should be translated by first checking:

options.text: Causality is established.
Design, confounding, selection, outcome and applicability.
Sex and gender should be ignored.
It is automatically a guideline.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Evidence design determines causal confidence. [MGB][CDC]

title: Vascular Medicine Fellowship

prerequisites.learnerLevel: Postgraduate physician self-study; intended for learners with internal medicine, cardiovascular physiology, vascular anatomy and evidence-appraisal foundations.
prerequisites.programmeSpecific: BWH invites physicians with prior ACGME-accredited cardiovascular or pulmonary/critical care fellowship; IM graduates may be considered individually. Verify current requirements directly.
prerequisites.scope: No independent diagnosis, procedures or unsupervised patient-care authorization.

objectives: Integrate vascular mechanisms and risk across arterial, venous, lymphatic and inflammatory disease.
Select and interpret common vascular diagnostic tests with limitations.
Apply board-domain knowledge to PAD, ALI/CLTI, cerebrovascular/visceral, aortic, VTE/PE and chronic venous disease.
Communicate urgency, referral and team-based care; use dated authoritative sources.
Apply privacy, equity and case/image-rights principles.

boardNames: American Board of Vascular Medicine (ABVM) Vascular Medicine examination/certification
Registered Physician in Vascular Interpretation (RPVI) credential (PVI exam; not a specialty board exam)
medical.boardStatus: A distinct APCA/Inteleos ABVM Vascular Medicine certification exam exists. Current criteria require unrestricted licensure, primary ABIM/AOBIM board certification and qualifying fellowship or practice pathway. BWH says fellows are eligible for the exam but individual prerequisites still apply. PVI is a separate examination leading to the RPVI interpretation credential, not the specialty board. No separate ABIM vascular medicine subspecialty exam was established in the sources reviewed.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This course grants no ABVM/RPVI eligibility. As checked 2026-10-07, ABVM requires unrestricted medical license, current ABIM/AOBIM primary certification, and a qualifying training pathway (including an eligible ≥12-month vascular medicine fellowship) or practice pathway. BWH invites physicians after accredited cardiovascular or pulmonary/critical-care fellowship; internal-medicine graduates may be individually considered. Verify current individual criteria with Inteleos/APCA and the programme.

officialProgrammes.name: BWH Vascular Medicine Fellowship (page titled “Vascular Medicine Training at Mass General Brigham”)
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official physician clinical fellowship describes inpatient consults, year-long ambulatory clinic, vascular lab, CT/MR/PET, catheter/interventional radiology and vascular surgery service, electives/away rotations across PAD, cerebrovascular, aortic, VTE, venous/lymphatic and pulmonary vascular disease, FMD, vasculitis and renovascular disease, plus scholarly activity. Says fellows are eligible to take ABVM exam. No didactic hour totals or program-specific ACGME accreditation claim published.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The supplied MED-X092 packet and saved supplemental-discovery record list one BWH clinical physician fellowship variant. It is clinical post-graduate training with scholarly activity, not a generic directory category, research-only job or nonphysician supplement. It is not vascular surgery, which has a separate ACGME programme type. The BWH page does not establish ACGME accreditation of this fellowship itself. No combined-program variant was found in the supplied record.
sourceCaveats: Official programme page does not disclose didactic video hours or state programme-specific ACGME accreditation.
ABVM requirements are individual and may change; RPVI is a different credential.
The older PAD lecture is conceptual only; use 2024 PAD and 2026 PE clinical guidance for current decisions.
SVM atlas public case availability was not established; Radiopaedia links are view-only and may not be redistributed. No source images/patient records were copied.

Independent self-study only; no affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, certification, case volume, procedural competence, or guaranteed pass. Human clinical review not performed.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has exertional calf symptoms, normal resting ABI, and persistent clinical suspicion. What next?

options.text: Dismiss PAD.
Exercise ABI to evaluate discordant symptoms.
Invasive angiography solely for diagnosis.
Diagnose CLTI.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Exercise ABI can help in suspected chronic symptomatic PAD with normal/borderline resting ABI. [6]

practiceQuestions.stem: A diabetic patient has ABI >1.40 and symptoms. Best interpretation?

options.text: Normal compressible arteries.
Noncompressible artery may falsely elevate ABI; consider toe pressure/TBI.
ALI by definition.
Venous reflux proven.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Calcification may prevent compression; use toe pressure/TBI in context. [6]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which set matches the 2024 PAD clinical subsets?

options.text: Silent, acute, aneurysmal, postprocedural.
Asymptomatic, chronic symptomatic, CLTI, ALI.
Venous, lymphatic, inflammatory, trauma.
Claudication, thrombophilia, dissection, vasculitis.

practiceQuestions.rationale: These are the four guideline-defined clinical subsets. [6]

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has a nonhealing ischemic toe wound for weeks. Best framework?

options.text: Wound alone dictates procedure.
Assess wound/ischemia/infection and coordinate multidisciplinary limb evaluation.
Any wound is ALI.
Exercise only.

practiceQuestions.rationale: CLTI and WIfI require integrated assessment and team-based care. [6]

practiceQuestions.stem: Which finding demands urgent evaluation rather than routine claudication workup?

options.text: Stable symptoms for months.
Sudden limb pain, coolness and new sensory/motor deficit.
Chronic mild edema.
Incidental asymptomatic plaque.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Acute hypoperfusion with neurologic findings may be limb-threatening. [6]

practiceQuestions.stem: For acute PE, which general current-guideline principle is appropriate?

options.text: Severity only from clot burden.
Integrate clinical status, hemodynamics, RV function and biomarkers in current framework.
D-dimer without pretest probability.
Same reperfusion for every patient.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Risk-stratified assessment is central to the 2026 adult PE guideline. [7]

practiceQuestions.stem: Sudden maximal-onset chest/back pain and pulse asymmetry: safest educational response?

options.text: Normal chest X-ray excludes acute aortic syndrome.

Unlikely under age 80.
Outpatient ABI first.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Acute aortic syndromes need urgent evaluation; plain film cannot rule out. [8]

Always infection.
Only lower limb veins.

practiceQuestions.rationale: FMD is nonatherosclerotic and noninflammatory. [9]

title: Vascular and Endovascular Surgery Fellowship
prerequisites: Advanced learner: physician/vascular-surgery trainee or surgeon with prior general-surgical training; assumes graduate-level anatomy, physiology, pathology, perioperative medicine and evidence appraisal.

Before advanced units, learners should be able to interpret basic arterial and venous anatomy, hemodynamics, duplex terminology, cross-sectional angiographic planes, renal function and common perioperative laboratory results.
This is an independent educational resource, not a prerequisite for clinical care, a substitute for an accredited 5+2 training programme, or an endorsement of unsupervised decisions or procedures.
objectives: Organize a vascular problem representation, prioritized differential, focused diagnostic workup and explicit escalation plan across arterial, venous and access disease.
Interpret vascular-laboratory and cross-sectional imaging at a conceptual level, identify limitations and correlate findings with symptoms, anatomy, physiology and renal/contrast risk.
Compare evidence-supported medical, open, endovascular and hybrid strategies while distinguishing urgent threats, patient risk, anatomy, durability, surveillance and patient goals.

Recognize complications and postoperative deterioration, including bleeding, acute limb ischemia, stroke, access failure, renal injury, compartment syndrome, infection and spinal-cord ischemia, and communicate the need for supervised/emergency evaluation.
Use the ABS 2025 vascular QE blueprint and SCORE curriculum as study maps; reason aloud in original non-official cases without treating course scores as exam predictions.
Appraise guideline currency, study design and outcome measures; use shared decision-making, privacy, teamwork, quality improvement and disclosure of uncertainty.

studyHours.plan: Illustrative self-study plan: 36 planned hours of future source-cited original recorded teaching; 48 hours reading and guideline comparison; 36 hours case and image interpretation on source sites; 20 hours question review and error log; 12 hours journal club/QI; 8 hours oral practice. boardNames: American Board of Surgery (ABS), Vascular Surgery primary certificate (Vascular Surgery Board administers examinations)
medical.boardStatus: A distinct ABS primary certificate in Vascular Surgery exists. Initial certification requires an approved training pathway and successful completion of both the Vascular Surgery Qualifying Examination (VSQE) and Vascular Surgery Certifying Examination (VSCE). The VSQE is the cognitive examination; the VSCE is an oral clinical-reasoning examination. The reviewed sources do not identify a separate endovascular-surgery board examination or certification; endovascular care is within vascular surgery training and assessment.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent educational curriculum confers no ABS/ABMS/ACGME status, board eligibility, licensure, operative privileges, procedural competence, credential, or guarantee of passing. ABS eligibility requires approved postgraduate training, documented supervised clinical experience and operative logs, and other current requirements. As checked 2026-10-07, the ABS lists 250 major vascular reconstructions, specified critical-care cases, ATLS plus ACLS/ALS for VSQE registration, RPVI certification and unrestricted U.S./Canadian medical licensure for VSCE registration; exact requirements can change. Independent/ESP candidates need an approved General Surgery QE application before VSQE access, but passing GSQE is not necessarily prerequisite to vascular certification. Consult ABS directly.

medical.programmeSourceScope: The supplied discovery packet lists both variants. BWH's programme page describes an independent post-general-surgery clinical fellowship; MGB's page explicitly names its independent fellowship. ABS defines the 5+2 independent route as five years of accredited general surgery followed by two accredited vascular-surgery years. ACGME's 2026 requirements specify 24 months for independent programs; these general accreditation requirements do not independently establish each listed program's current accreditation status. The BWH page carries an ACGME tag; live ACGME registry status was not separately confirmed. The 0+5 integrated pathway is a distinct route and is not silently substituted for this fellowship. No research-only or non-physician track is included.
sourceCaveats: Institutional pages are programme descriptions, not a full published didactic syllabus or guarantee of individual accreditation status. Preserve BWH and MGB programme variants.

The ABS Vascular Surgery primary certificate is separate from the General Surgery certificate; the 5+2 path can lead to both. Independent candidates need an approved GSQE application, but ABS says passing GSQE is not a prerequisite for vascular certification. There are separate vascular VSQE/VSCE exams; no separate endovascular-specific board exam was identified.
The public ABS page reflects current online rules checked on 2026-10-07; verify before decisions because board rules can change. ACGME requirements are not board eligibility rules.

SVS-linked publications and tools vary in free access; no logins were bypassed. ESVS public page describes a free guidelines app. Some Radiopaedia case pages were blocked by an anti-bot challenge; no workaround was attempted.

A search-indexed YouTube item is not counted as free ready video without observed public playback and runtime. Metadata extraction failed or returned a bot challenge; therefore verified external lecture time remains zero, with a full 36-hour verified-video gap. Planned clips are production goals only.
No clinical image, recording, proprietary question, patient record or complete guideline figure is copied into these files. Free viewing does not grant reuse rights.

Human clinical review is NOT PERFORMED. Independent education does not grant affiliation, accredited training, licensure, board eligibility, procedure competence, certification or guaranteed exam success.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient with diabetes and advanced kidney disease has a nonhealing toe ulcer. The ankle arteries are poorly compressible and the ABI is unexpectedly high despite monophasic pedal Doppler signals. Which next step best addresses the unresolved perfusion question?

options.text: Treat the ABI as proof of normal perfusion
Obtain toe pressure/toe-brachial or another appropriate physiologic assessment and correlate clinically
Diagnose CLTI from the ulcer alone
Proceed directly to intervention without further assessment

practiceQuestions.rationale: Medial calcification can make ankle pressures noncompressible and falsely reassuring. Toe-level or alternative physiologic measures and clinical correlation can clarify perfusion; the ulcer alone does not establish ischemia or dictate treatment.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional patient with suspected chronic limb-threatening ischemia, what best describes the purpose of WIfI staging?

options.text: It independently mandates a particular operation
It organizes wound, ischemia and foot-infection severity to communicate limb threat and inform decisions
It replaces objective perfusion testing
It is a validated guarantee of wound healing

practiceQuestions.rationale: WIfI is a staging/communication framework. It should inform but not replace clinical judgment, objective assessment, patient risk, anatomy and preferences.

practiceQuestions.stem: A CTA in a fictional patient with Stanford type B dissection shows one renal artery from the false lumen and another visceral branch from the true lumen. What is the most useful immediate interpretive step?

options.text: Ignore branch origins because all type B dissections are anatomically equivalent
Map the dissection extent, true/false lumen and branch perfusion, then correlate with organ function and symptoms
Assume every false-lumen branch is occluded
Classify it as type A solely because a renal branch is involved

practiceQuestions.rationale: Branch origins and perfusion help assess malperfusion and plan multidisciplinary evaluation. Stanford classification depends on ascending-aortic involvement, not renal branch involvement alone.

practiceQuestions.stem: A hypothetical patient after EVAR has a surveillance study raising concern for an endoleak. Which response best reflects sound reasoning?

options.text: Discontinue surveillance if symptoms are absent
Characterize the finding using the appropriate imaging and current surveillance guidance, considering sac behavior, anatomy and renal/contrast risk
Assume any endoleak has the same significance and requires the same treatment
Rely only on a normal physical examination

practiceQuestions.rationale: Post-EVAR surveillance is important, and evaluation depends on endoleak type, sac change, anatomy and patient factors. Do not make a single management decision without appropriate specialist review and current guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient develops sudden severe leg pain, pallor and new sensory change. What is the best high-level priority?

options.text: Schedule routine outpatient follow-up
Treat as a potential acute limb threat and escalate urgently for in-person assessment by the responsible clinical team
Assume chronic claudication because peripheral artery disease is common
Wait for a lecture or online advice before contacting clinicians

practiceQuestions.rationale: Sudden pain with sensory change can indicate acute limb ischemia and needs urgent clinical assessment. This educational item does not prescribe a procedure or substitute for emergency care.
practiceQuestions.domain: Lower extremity; urgency and patient care

practiceQuestions.stem: A fictional patient has weeks of postprandial abdominal pain and weight loss. Which approach is most appropriate for a vascular-surgery learner's initial reasoning?

options.text: Assume chronic mesenteric ischemia without a differential or imaging review
Build a differential, correlate symptoms and risk with appropriate mesenteric imaging, and seek timely specialist evaluation if concern persists
Dismiss vascular causes if a routine abdominal exam is benign
Treat an incidental stenosis as proof of causality

practiceQuestions.rationale: Chronic mesenteric ischemia requires correlation of compatible symptoms and vascular anatomy while considering alternative causes; an incidental lesion alone does not establish causality.

practiceQuestions.stem: In a fictional hemodialysis-access imaging case, duplex shows low access flow and focal outflow stenoses. What is the most defensible interpretation?

options.text: A single low-flow measurement proves access irreversibility
Stenosis or thrombosis in inflow/outflow can contribute to access dysfunction; correlate with symptoms, anatomy and the dialysis team's assessment
Outflow lesions never affect access function
The image alone authorizes an unsupervised intervention

practiceQuestions.rationale: Access dysfunction can arise from inflow or outflow stenosis/thrombosis; symptoms, examination, duplex and dialysis context are integrated. The case image is educational and does not authorize treatment.

practiceQuestions.stem: After a fictional knee dislocation, a patient has a diminished distal pulse. What is the best principle for the next step?

options.text: Exclude arterial injury because the pulse is present
Recognize possible popliteal injury, reassess perfusion and use the trauma team's urgent diagnostic pathway
Delay assessment until swelling resolves
Assume the finding is chronic PAD

practiceQuestions.rationale: Knee dislocation can be associated with popliteal arterial injury. A pulse does not reliably exclude injury; urgent structured assessment and escalation are appropriate.

practiceQuestions.stem: A quality-improvement team reports fewer graft infections after a new protocol in a small before-after series. What is the most important first appraisal question?

options.text: Was a causal effect proven because the rate fell?
What were the case definitions, denominator, time period, baseline differences, co-interventions and balancing measures?
Can the outcome be ignored because the sample is small?
Should all sites adopt the protocol without local review?

practiceQuestions.rationale: A before-after association may be confounded by changes in case mix, ascertainment or concurrent interventions. Define measures and limits before inferring cause or generalizing.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement about U.S. vascular-surgery certification is accurate as checked 2026-10-07?

options.text: A free online course alone grants vascular board eligibility
ABS vascular certification uses a VSQE and a VSCE after approved training; this self-study course grants neither eligibility nor certification
The VSITE is a publicly available individual board-certification exam
A separate endovascular-surgery board examination is required in addition to vascular certification

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABS describes two vascular certification exams, with approved pathway and other requirements. VSITE is an in-training exam furnished to programmes and is not a certification requirement; no separate endovascular board exam was identified in the reviewed official sources.

medical.boardStatus: ABIM certifies Interventional Cardiology, with a separate exam and formal eligibility requirements. No separate Complex PCI/CHIP board exam identified. ABIM requires prior Cardiovascular Disease certification, qualifying accredited interventional training, documented minimum procedures, competence, unrestricted license and passing the exam. The CHIP fellowship is classified non-ACGME in supplied packet; completion does not establish eligibility.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: Independent course completion, or a non-ACGME complex-PCI fellowship alone, is not evidence of ABIM exam eligibility; ABIM decides under current policy.

officialProgrammes.name: Mass General Brigham PCI Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official heading is Complex and High-Risk Indicated Procedure (CHIP) PCI Fellowship. Two fellows rotate quarterly between MGH and BWH; if one is recruited, time is split. Entry requires completed general cardiology fellowship and at least one year of interventional cardiology fellowship. Page describes CTO, complex/high-risk PCI, imaging, MCS, Heart Team and research. Page does not call this track ACGME-accredited; supplied packet classifies it non-ACGME. MGB separately lists a one-year ACGME-accredited interventional cardiology fellowship.

medical.programmeSourceScope: One distinct clinical physician fellowship from the supplied institutional variant; not a generic directory category, combined board program, research-only role or non-physician supplement. Preserve MGB name and MGH/BWH rotation-site wording. Public pages do not supply a complete private lecture set, case log or training outcomes.

ABIM blueprint categories are typical weights, not exact exam promises.
2025 ACS guideline and 2026 radiation consensus were checked. Revascularization link is the official 2021 page; check for later updates.
MCS consensus referenced is 2015 and cannot be a sole current authority.
42 specialty videos passed public metadata checks; direct player playback not sampled for every item. Two HTTP 401 candidates excluded. No duplicate IDs or planned films count.
Public video access does not grant content/image reuse rights. ACC/Frontiers case pages did not establish formal case de-identification; link only.
Human clinical review not performed. Independent education does not grant affiliation, accreditation, licensure, eligibility, competence or certification.

title: Emergency Sports Medicine Fellowship
level: Clinical physician fellowship (institutional emergency-medicine sports medicine track; not a separate residency specialty)-aligned independent study

prerequisites.learnerLevel: Advanced physician self-study, designed for EM residency graduates and sports medicine fellows; not a substitute for clinical practice.
prerequisites.required: Prior emergency medicine physician training is assumed for clinical context; learners should already know resuscitation fundamentals. Maintain current clinical certifications separately.
prerequisites.recommended: Anatomy, exercise physiology, acute musculoskeletal evaluation, ECG fundamentals, concussion recognition, medical statistics and emergency team communication.
prerequisites.limits: No clinical clearance, independent care, imaging interpretation credential, ultrasound competency, procedure authorization, or unsupervised event coverage results.

objectives: Map this institutional clinical track to emergency-medicine physician fellowship versus sports-medicine CAQ and distinguish programme listing from accreditation and board eligibility.
Apply board-blueprint-weighted knowledge to athlete prevention, acute emergencies, orthopaedic injury and general medical conditions.
Construct a team-based emergency response plan and clear handoff using current local protocols.
Reason through an athlete’s differential and escalation without making unsupported diagnoses.
Critically assess public clinical cases and images under copyright and privacy constraints.
Design a learning/quality-improvement plan and identify when clinical review, supervision or referral is required.

units.title: Emergency sports medicine role, evidence, and team systems
objectives: Distinguish emergency sports medicine fellowship track from core specialty, sports-medicine fellowship and CAQ.
Use role clarity, handoffs, documentation, consent, privacy, and evidence appraisal.
topics: Program identity; team physician duties; shared decisions; consent; negligence concepts; evidence hierarchy; equity and access.
casePractice: Create a one-page scope/role map separating ED, team, event, athletic-trainer, EMS, and subspecialist tasks.
assessment: Scored 0-2 for scope accuracy, evidence quality, and referral/communication safety; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Preparticipation evaluation and cardiovascular risk
objectives: Structure a PPE around history and focused examination; identify red flags for deferral/referral.
Interpret athlete ECG context cautiously and specify limits of screening.
topics: PPE purpose; sudden cardiac death differential; exertional syncope, chest pain, family history, ECG; shared clearance; state/sport variation.
casePractice: Analyze an openly posted AMSSM ECG teaching case and write a differential, urgency, and next-step plan without treating a single ECG finding as a diagnosis.
assessment: 0-2 each for history/risk signals, differential and limits, disposition/communication; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Event medicine, emergency action plans and field triage
objectives: Construct venue-specific written emergency action plan (EAP) with assigned roles, access, equipment, activation, EMS handoff and rehearsals.
Prioritize ABC threats, remove from play, and communicate transport decisions.
topics: EAP, AED access, EMS interface, mass gatherings, commotio cordis, airway, major hemorrhage, cervical-spine concerns.
casePractice: Draft a one-page venue EAP plus a 90-second handoff for suspected catastrophic cardiac event.
assessment: 0-2 for venue specificity, executable role/EMS/AED pathway, practice/debrief plan; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Collapse, cardiac arrest and acute cardiopulmonary emergencies
objectives: Differentiate immediately life-threatening causes of collapse without premature closure.
Apply current resuscitation algorithms only within current certification, team, equipment and local protocol.
topics: Sudden cardiac arrest, exertional collapse, arrhythmia, asthma/exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, anaphylaxis, pulmonary embolism and pneumothorax.
casePractice: Use a fictional collapsed-runner scenario to write an ABC-first differential, activation plan, and evidence-limited disposition.
assessment: 0-2 for rapid threat identification, differential, escalation and handoff; pass >=6/8.

units.title: Heat illness, cold injury, altitude and exertional rhabdomyolysis
objectives: Recognize exertional heat stroke as a time-critical diagnosis and distinguish it from other exertional heat illness.
Explain rectal core-temperature measurement and on-site cooling priorities; avoid unsupported precise prescriptions.
topics: EHS vs heat exhaustion/syncope/cramps; WBGT/acclimatization; cooling-first framework; cold injury; altitude; rhabdomyolysis differential.
casePractice: Submit a heat illness decision tree and defend why skin feel/sweating is not a reliable exclusion criterion.
assessment: 0-2 for differentiating syndrome, evidence-supported emergency priorities, limits/referral; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Concussion, neurologic and spine emergencies
objectives: Identify danger signs after head/neck injury and distinguish emergency referral from uncomplicated suspected concussion.
Apply a graduated, symptom-guided return-to-sport framework with clinical supervision and jurisdictional rules.
topics: Concussion assessment; red flags; cervical spine trauma; seizure/syncope mimics; school/work supports; return to learn/play; persistent symptoms.
casePractice: Complete a fictional concussion timeline with red flags, referral triggers and conditional return progression; do not clear a real athlete.
assessment: 0-2 for danger signs, staged plan, safeguarding and documentation; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Acute musculoskeletal assessment and imaging
objectives: Use mechanism, focused exam, neurovascular status and decision rules to prioritize differential and imaging/referral.
Recognize limb- or life-threatening conditions including dislocation with vascular compromise and compartment syndrome.
topics: Knee, shoulder, elbow, hand/wrist, hip, ankle/foot; fracture/dislocation; occult injury; exam limits; plain films and advanced imaging indications.
casePractice: Write a structured injury note for a fictional knee injury including mechanism, focused findings, imaging question and escalation.
assessment: 0-2 for targeted history/exam, dangerous differential, imaging/consult logic; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Musculoskeletal ultrasound and procedure safety
objectives: Explain the role and limits of diagnostic sports ultrasound and distinguish imaging education from credentialed procedural competence.
Describe consent, infection prevention, supervision and escalation for procedures.
topics: Ultrasound physics, normal/pathology, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hip/knee/ankle; dynamic assessment; injections/aspiration boundaries.
casePractice: View free AMSSM modules if accessible; annotate a publicly linked case and state what ultrasound cannot establish alone.
assessment: 0-2 for modality limitations, anatomy/correlation, safety and scope; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Sports trauma by region, pediatric athlete and growth plate
objectives: Build a prioritized region-based differential with age and skeletal maturity considered.
Identify pediatric red flags, physeal/apophyseal injury patterns and specialist referral needs.
topics: Shoulder/elbow/hand; spine; pelvis/hip/thigh; knee; leg/ankle/foot; growth plate and apophysis; overuse and bone stress.
casePractice: Compare two fictional adolescent injury pathways and identify imaging/referral questions without asserting a diagnosis from a resource image.
assessment: 0-2 for age-specific reasoning, competing diagnoses, escalation; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Medical conditions in active participants
objectives: Recognize common systemic illness presentations in active people and screen for emergency warning signs.
Use medications, history, exposure and sport context in a differential without assuming exercise explains symptoms.
topics: Hematology/sickle cell considerations; diabetes; asthma; GI/GU; infectious/skin disease; endocrine; mental health; medication/supplement and anti-doping literacy.
casePractice: Use a fictional exertional symptoms case to outline medication, disease, exposure and safeguarding questions, then state urgent referral criteria.
assessment: 0-2 for breadth, triage, medication/consent privacy, uncertainty; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Return-to-sport reasoning, rehabilitation, prevention and longitudinal care
objectives: Use explicit criteria, function, sport demands, patient goals and shared decisions in return-to-sport plans.
Avoid calendar-only clearance and communicate conditionality and re-evaluation triggers.
topics: Rehabilitation principles; load progression; injury prevention; recurrence; pain; return to learn/play/work; patient-centered shared decisions.
casePractice: Prepare a staged fictional return-to-training plan with objective milestones, red flags and stop criteria.
assessment: 0-2 for criteria, individualization, monitoring and clear communication; pass >=5/6.

units.title: Research, administration, mass events and quality improvement
objectives: Critically appraise a sports medicine study and translate a finding into a cautious practice question.
Propose event coverage/quality measures and close the loop after incidents.
topics: Research design; measurement; bias; event administration; mass-participation care; handoffs; quality improvement; reporting and debrief.
casePractice: Create a small PDSA proposal for EAP rehearsal or event triage, with process/outcome/balancing measures.
assessment: 0-2 for question/design, feasible metric, privacy/safety and learning cycle; pass >=5/6.

assignment.title: Fictional event-to-clinic case conference and EAP audit
deliverables: A fictional, de-identified-by-construction case narrative (never derived from a real patient record), documenting differential and red flags.
A venue-specific one-page EAP audit with roles, access, equipment, EMS coordination, rehearsal and debrief.
A 500-800 word evidence map linking clinical assertions to current sources and uncertainties.
A conditional return-to-activity plan for an uncomplicated fictional concussion and a separate escalation plan for red flags.

rubric.proficient: Threat-first, immediate emergency action, appropriate uncertainty, referral/EMS triggers.
Balanced differential; distinguishes screening, diagnosis and management; uses current authoritative references.
Specific executable EAP, handoff, roles, access and debrief.
Maps domains accurately and does not claim exam readiness.
Links only, no clinical image copying, no unauthorized case records, no competence/clearance claim.

assignment.passCriterion: At least 80/100 with no critical safety failure. The rubric is instructional, not validated.

assessment.format: 12-unit formative cases, 10 original single-best-answer practice questions, a case conference and one EAP/QI assignment.
assessment.standard: Practice only, not official test items, not a validated exam predictor, and not a passing-readiness measure. Each learner must verify current guidance and local laws.

studyHours.plan: Illustrative study plan: 12 units x 3-4 hours of reading/cases (36-48 h), 7.80 h verified lectures, 8-12 h for assignments and question review (total about 52-68 h). Individual time varies; this is not clinical training time or a board-readiness claim.

unitMap.text: Emergency sports medicine role, evidence, and team systems
coveredTopics: Program identity; team physician duties; shared decisions; consent; negligence concepts; evidence hierarchy; equity and access.

unitMap.text: Preparticipation evaluation and cardiovascular risk
coveredTopics: PPE purpose; sudden cardiac death differential; exertional syncope, chest pain, family history, ECG; shared clearance; state/sport variation.

unitMap.text: Event medicine, emergency action plans and field triage
coveredTopics: EAP, AED access, EMS interface, mass gatherings, commotio cordis, airway, major hemorrhage, cervical-spine concerns.

unitMap.text: Collapse, cardiac arrest and acute cardiopulmonary emergencies
coveredTopics: Sudden cardiac arrest, exertional collapse, arrhythmia, asthma/exercise-induced bronchoconstriction, anaphylaxis, pulmonary embolism and pneumothorax.

unitMap.text: Heat illness, cold injury, altitude and exertional rhabdomyolysis
coveredTopics: EHS vs heat exhaustion/syncope/cramps; WBGT/acclimatization; cooling-first framework; cold injury; altitude; rhabdomyolysis differential.

unitMap.text: Concussion, neurologic and spine emergencies
coveredTopics: Concussion assessment; red flags; cervical spine trauma; seizure/syncope mimics; school/work supports; return to learn/play; persistent symptoms.

unitMap.text: Acute musculoskeletal assessment and imaging
coveredTopics: Knee, shoulder, elbow, hand/wrist, hip, ankle/foot; fracture/dislocation; occult injury; exam limits; plain films and advanced imaging indications.

unitMap.text: Musculoskeletal ultrasound and procedure safety
coveredTopics: Ultrasound physics, normal/pathology, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hip/knee/ankle; dynamic assessment; injections/aspiration boundaries.

unitMap.text: Sports trauma by region, pediatric athlete and growth plate
coveredTopics: Shoulder/elbow/hand; spine; pelvis/hip/thigh; knee; leg/ankle/foot; growth plate and apophysis; overuse and bone stress.

unitMap.text: Medical conditions in active participants
coveredTopics: Hematology/sickle cell considerations; diabetes; asthma; GI/GU; infectious/skin disease; endocrine; mental health; medication/supplement and anti-doping literacy.

unitMap.text: Return-to-sport reasoning, rehabilitation, prevention and longitudinal care
coveredTopics: Rehabilitation principles; load progression; injury prevention; recurrence; pain; return to learn/play/work; patient-centered shared decisions.

unitMap.text: Research, administration, mass events and quality improvement
coveredTopics: Research design; measurement; bias; event administration; mass-participation care; handoffs; quality improvement; reporting and debrief.

topicGaps: Verified public recordings reviewed do not cover the full emergency sports medicine/2026 CAQ blueprint. Notably underrepresented: PPE/cardiac screening, venue EAP practice, broad non-knee MSK anatomy, pediatric growth-plate injury, common chronic/sports medical conditions, ultrasound didactics, rehabilitation and team-physician governance.
Do not interpret AMSSM’s public ultrasound modules as counted until each video runtime and anonymous free playback are checked.
No public MGB lecture recordings or its complete official didactic sequence were found; do not fabricate institution-specific lectures.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardStatus.physicianSpecialtyStatus: Sports Medicine is a clinical subspecialty/CAQ, not a standalone physician residency specialty. Emergency Sports Medicine is the specific institutional fellowship label for a clinical EM-graduate track. It is not the same as a generic sports medicine directory category.
boardStatus.exam: Sports Medicine CAQ/ABEM SPM Certification Examination; ABFM develops/administers the examination, ABEM credentials eligible ABEM candidates.
boardStatus.programmeAccreditation: MGB says its one-year programme fulfills all ACGME requirements for Sports Medicine CAQ board eligibility. The official programme page reviewed did not expressly label the specific MGB programme ACGME-accredited; independent current accreditation verification was not obtained. ABEM eligibility requires completion of an ACGME-accredited programme, so the wording is not treated as proof of individual eligibility.

medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent course does not confer board eligibility. The MGB page says the fellowship fulfills ACGME requirements for Sports Medicine CAQ eligibility. ABEM requires qualifying underlying certification, continuing certification, medical licensure and successful completion of an ACGME-accredited sports-medicine fellowship. Specific current site accreditation and an individual’s eligibility were not independently verified. Check with ABEM/ABFM and programme officials. Passing the examination is not guaranteed.

officialProgrammes.name: MGB Emergency Sports Medicine Fellowship
officialProgrammes.publicCurriculumNotes: Official page describes a one-year fellowship for emergency-medicine residency graduates; emphasis on pre-hospital care; objectives describe sports/orthopaedic/cardiology clinics, ED, events, ultrasound, research, administration and mentorship. Page states it fulfills ACGME requirements for Sports Medicine CAQ board eligibility. No detailed block calendar, exact didactic hours, procedure/case minimums or separate current accreditation finding published on the page.

medical.programmeSourceScope: This single public institutional offering is retained with its exact name. No separate generic sports-medicine programme, combined residency, non-physician certification, or research-only postdoctoral appointment is included. MGB’s official offer is the clinical EM-fellowship track; avoid generalizing its name into a board specialty or asserting accreditation absent a direct listing.
sourceCaveats: MGB official page supports a one-year clinical physician fellowship intended for EM residency graduates, not a research-only or non-physician programme.
Institutional phrase “fulfills all ACGME requirements” is preserved, but it is not silently upgraded to an independently verified ACGME accreditation finding.
The current ABFM Sports Medicine blueprint effective Jan. 1 2026 is used for board-domain weighting; the detailed older ABFM content outline is supplemental topic detail only.

ABEM’s separate sports medicine subspecialty examination exists. Eligibility depends on underlying certification, program accreditation, licensure, and continuing certification; no individual eligibility determination is made.

The eight video entries each have unique YouTube IDs. Repeated subject area heat includes one broad heat-illness lecture and one later heat-stroke lecture; their distinct IDs and distinct scope are counted once each.

Durations observed on public YouTube page; anonymous page/player metadata was visible, but this research process did not stream playback. Excluded ultrasound and AMSSM member-area playlist content with unknown runtime/access.
Free view does not license copying. Authenticity or de-identification of AMSSM cases/images was not independently attested; links only.
Current medical practice changes. NATA 2015 heat statement and AMSSM environmental reference last updated 2022 are dated sources; cross-check newer guidelines and local protocols.

This independent self-study course is unaffiliated and unaccredited; it does not replace training, licensure, board eligibility, certification or supervised clinical/procedural competency. No human clinical review was performed.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which programme description is supported by MGB’s published page?

options.text: A standalone ABMS specialty residency
A one-year fellowship for EM residency graduates with clinical/event and other experiences
A research-only postdoctoral appointment
A non-physician athletic training certification

practiceQuestions.rationale: MGB describes a one-year fellowship designed for emergency-medicine residency graduates and clinical, ultrasound, event, research and administrative experience. [1]

practiceQuestions.stem: A candidate asks whether completing this named fellowship automatically qualifies them for ABEM Sports Medicine certification. Best response?

options.text: Yes, all graduates qualify
No; eligibility requires the relevant base-board status, continuing certification, licensure, and an eligible ACGME-accredited fellowship; verify the specific programme and candidate with ABEM
Only a sports medicine course is required
Board status is irrelevant

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABEM’s published criteria impose multiple candidate and fellowship conditions. MGB’s statement that it fulfills ACGME requirements does not, by itself, independently document current accreditation or guarantee any individual’s eligibility. [3][4]

practiceQuestions.stem: The CAQ’s separate examination status is best stated as:

options.text: There is no examination
ABFM administers a sports-medicine certification examination; ABEM credentials eligible EM candidates and co-sponsors the pathway
It is a general medical licensing exam
The ACGME certifies individual fellows

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABEM explicitly describes the SPM certification exam, and ABFM says the CAQ requires passing the one-day examination. [3][5]

practiceQuestions.stem: During PPE, an asymptomatic competitive athlete has a concerning family history of premature sudden death and exertional syncope. Best next step?

options.text: Unrestricted clearance based on normal appearance
Defer unrestricted participation and arrange focused cardiovascular evaluation under current guidance
Diagnose hypertrophic cardiomyopathy immediately
Recommend universal ECG-based diagnosis without context

practiceQuestions.rationale: Red flags require further risk assessment and an individualized plan; PPE does not establish a diagnosis. Screening strategy and rules vary by context. [12]

practiceQuestions.stem: An athlete collapses during intense exercise, is confused and hot. Which principle is most appropriate?

options.text: Assume dehydration and give oral fluids only
Treat as a time-critical emergency, activate venue EAP/EMS, assess core temperature with an appropriate method and initiate rapid on-site cooling for suspected EHS
Wait for laboratory confirmation before cooling
Use skin moisture to exclude heat stroke

practiceQuestions.rationale: NATA/AMSSM resources emphasize emergency action and prompt cooling for suspected exertional heat stroke; diagnosis and care require trained clinicians and local protocols. [10][11]

practiceQuestions.stem: The strongest documented practical distinction between concussion progression steps is:

options.text: Move forward despite new symptoms
Advance only if no new symptoms at current exertion level; stop and contact provider if symptoms recur, with clinical supervision and required clearance
Return to competition after 24 hours regardless of symptoms
Use a single cognitive score as clearance

practiceQuestions.rationale: CDC describes gradual progression, monitoring symptoms and clinical provider supervision/clearance. [7][8]

practiceQuestions.stem: A field emergency action plan is most complete when it:

options.text: Is generic and only stored in the medical director’s office
Is venue-specific with roles, access/equipment, EMS coordination, rehearsal, distribution, and post-event review
Names only a phone number
Substitutes a physician’s presence for rehearsed systems

practiceQuestions.rationale: NATA recommends a venue-specific EAP with interdisciplinary development, role clarity, coordination, annual rehearsal and review. [9]

practiceQuestions.stem: A young athlete has focal pain near an apophysis after repetitive throwing. The best reasoning approach is:

options.text: Assume adult tendon disease
Include growth-related injury in age- and maturity-sensitive differential; assess red flags and imaging/referral needs
Clear to play if pain improves during warmup
Use a single ultrasound view to prove the diagnosis

practiceQuestions.rationale: Skeletal maturity changes the injury differential; a teaching plan should preserve uncertainty and use appropriate clinical assessment rather than assert diagnosis from one image. [2][6]

practiceQuestions.stem: What does a freely viewable AMSSM ultrasound teaching video authorize?

options.text: Reposting the video and patient images
Using the link for study; no copying/rehosting absent a license
Using images in any commercial course
Certify procedural competence

practiceQuestions.rationale: Free access is not a republication license or competence credential. AMSSM describes free modules but gives no blanket reuse rights. [14]

practiceQuestions.stem: An athlete with exercise-associated collapse has no established cause yet. Which response best avoids premature closure?

options.text: Label heat exhaustion immediately
Start with ABCs, activate emergency response as indicated, consider cardiac, neurologic, environmental, metabolic and traumatic causes, and reassess
Clear once awake
Assume an athletic heart is benign

practiceQuestions.rationale: Collapsed-athlete differential and emergency response require systematic threat-first assessment; the lecture is educational and not a treatment protocol. [18][9]

Clinical photography, consent, patient goals, competing risks

High-risk site/border/recurrent disease; margin control
Advanced BCC and multidisciplinary options

coveredTopics: AAD guideline scope and high-risk MMS recommendation
BWH risk factors versus AJCC staging; clinical limits
Nodal evaluation, imaging, adjuvant radiation/systemic therapy and surveillance

unitMap.text: Rare and aggressive cutaneous tumors
coveredTopics: Representative histology and diagnostic uncertainty
MCC nodal and systemic context; immunotherapy is not interchangeable with local surgery
Margin control, immunostains, pathology collaboration and referral

unitMap.text: Melanoma and melanoma in situ
coveredTopics: Breslow depth, ulceration and diagnostic biopsy adequacy
Wide local excision and sentinel lymph node considerations
Lentigo maligna/MIS margin assessment and limits of extrapolating Mohs

unitMap.text: Mohs appropriateness, selection, and consent
coveredTopics: Indication versus convenience; tissue sparing and margin control
Patient/site/tumor factors; uncertainties and alternatives
Consent, expectations, goals, access and referral

unitMap.text: Perioperative evaluation, anesthesia, and safety
coveredTopics: Comorbidity and medication review; anticoagulation risk assessment
Asepsis, local/regional anesthesia, hemostasis and emergency response
Post-operative instructions, wound healing and adverse-event recognition

unitMap.text: Specimen acquisition and frozen-section laboratory
coveredTopics: Beveled/releasing technique, color coding, mapping and orientation
En-face processing, frozen sections, artifacts, recuts and immunostains
Lab setup, CLIA/OSHA/HIPAA and quality checks; operator competence requires supervision

unitMap.text: Slide interpretation and margin mapping
coveredTopics: Peripheral/deep margin visualization and histologic patterns
Mapping and correlation with clinical anatomy
Debulk specimens, recuts, stains, discordance and pathologist consultation

unitMap.text: Reconstruction after tumor clearance
coveredTopics: Anatomy-aware defect assessment; nose, eyelid, lip, ear and cheek
Advancement, rotation, transposition, interpolation, pedicled and graft choices
Staged repair, tissue expansion, scar revision and complications

unitMap.text: Nonsurgical, radiation, and systemic oncology
coveredTopics: Low-risk disease and nonsurgical alternatives; field therapies
Radiation and adjuvant use; contraindications and tradeoffs
Systemic therapy for advanced BCC/cSCC, melanoma, MCC and other tumors

unitMap.text: Follow-up, complications, practice systems, and board synthesis
coveredTopics: Wound complications, recurrence surveillance, prevention and survivorship
Coding, documentation, consent, ethics, HIPAA/CLIA/OSHA and quality improvement
Tumor board/referral, evidence appraisal and board-style synthesis

topicGaps: 33.4472 additional unique actual free video hours are not presently verified. High-priority shortfall: full professional-level BCC/cSCC risk and staging, melanoma/rare tumors, perioperative decisions, mapped specimen/laboratory management, frozen-section histology, repair design, systemic/radiation alternatives, complications, regulation/coding, and sufficient full-depth course time.

The ABD guide identifies all these broad content areas, but was linked through a 2024 page while the PDF itself says last updated May 2, 2019. A current complete public ABD blueprint/detailed MDS content weighting was not located.

The two counted recordings are not a complete board review: Mohs cryotomy overview (0.6375 h) and public Mohs department webinar (1.9153 h). A 1:03 ASDS course promotional video was excluded because it is a trailer for an on-demand course, not course lectures; course access may require purchase/member account.
remainingGaps.clinicalSkills: Supervised accredited clinical training is not supplied by these videos.

boardNames: American Board of Dermatology (ABD) – Micrographic Dermatologic Surgery (MDS) subspecialty certification examination
medical.boardStatus: An actual clinical physician subspecialty fellowship exists, with ACGME accreditation identified by official institutions and ABD. The American Board of Dermatology administers a separate MDS subspecialty certification exam/certificate; this is not a separate independent specialty board. ABD states that for 2026 onward, candidates must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship; the prior practice pathway ended after 2025. No second separate MDS board examination was identified. General dermatology certification prerequisites and individual exam eligibility remain governed by ABD.
medical.boardEligibilityNotice: This independent self-study course does not confer dermatology board certification, MDS eligibility, credentialing, or exam access. As of the ABD notice checked 2026-10-07, completion of an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship is required for the MDS exam beginning with the 2026 administration. ABD determines candidate-specific eligibility; verify current ABD rules.

medical.programmeSourceScope: Exact official institutional fellowship pages plus ABD fellowship/certification materials and ACGME requirements. These are real physician clinical fellowship variants, not a generic dermatology directory label or a research-only/non-physician supplement. MGH calls its offering one year; BWH lists a two-year program with optional MPH/research. ABD identifies the standard accredited fellowship as 12 months. The public pages do not expose complete curricula or clinical volumes.
sourceCaveats: ACGME’s newly posted interim MSDO requirement revision is dated September 28, 2026 but takes effect July 1, 2027; it is cited for forthcoming curriculum context, not represented as already effective.
The 2024 ABD guide page links a PDF whose own last-updated notice says May 2, 2019. Its board outline is useful but not guaranteed complete/current; current exam rules remain with ABD.

AAD cSCC guideline and cited BCC review are older publications. Use live current specialty guidance and multidisciplinary review before real clinical decisions; proprietary NCCN clinician guidelines were not copied or used as a free source.

Institutional pages establish offerings and public program descriptions, not complete official curriculum, patient volumes, equivalence, or individual trainee eligibility. No current dynamic ACGME public ADS roster query was conducted.

Mohs-image case content is original clinical imagery hosted by DermNet, but course authors did not independently audit the subject’s de-identification or consent. Links only; no photographs or patient records copied.

Public video access and runtime are snapshots at 2026-10-07 and may change. The Mohs-technique video page did not identify its uploader via stateless extraction. No rights to download, embed, reuse, slides, or rehost are implied.
No claim of guaranteed passing, clinical competence, procedure volume, or treatment result is made. Human clinical review was not performed.
