medical.sourceReviewNote: Source-cited research and automated checks; not clinician validation or exam-passing prediction.

practiceQuestions.stem: A recurrent infiltrative BCC is poorly defined on the nasal ala after prior excision. Which principle best supports discussing Mohs?

options.text: A high-risk recurrent tumor at a functionally and cosmetically sensitive site is a classic setting to consider complete margin assessment and tissue conservation.
All BCCs require Mohs, irrespective of site or risk.
Mohs is contraindicated after prior excision.
AUC makes Mohs mandatory for every patient in this category.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Risk features and site support considering margin-controlled surgery, but an individual decision includes patient context, alternatives, and current local standards. AUC is not a mandate and all BCC does not require Mohs.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement most accurately describes AAD guidance for high-risk cSCC in the open 2018 guideline?

options.text: Mohs micrographic surgery is recommended for high-risk cSCC.
Mohs is never appropriate for cSCC.
Every low-risk cSCC must receive Mohs.
The guideline covers mucosal head-and-neck SCC.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The guideline recommends MMS for high-risk cSCC; it distinguishes low-risk options and explicitly excludes mucosal SCC. This is a 2018 guideline and must be reconciled with current guidance.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description correctly distinguishes BWH cSCC risk stratification from AJCC staging?

options.text: BWH uses defined tumor risk factors for localized prognostic grouping; AJCC is a formal staging system and addresses broader stage categories.
BWH is the universal staging system for all skin cancers.
BWH and AJCC are interchangeable and never disagree.
Neither system uses histopathologic risk features.

practiceQuestions.rationale: AAD discusses BWH’s localized prognostic role and AJCC stage system separately; they are not interchangeable and have different intended uses.

practiceQuestions.stem: A patient with a primary invasive cutaneous melanoma 0.9 mm thick and clinically node-negative asks whether regional node status is relevant. Which is the best educational statement?

options.text: NCI describes consideration of lymphatic mapping and sentinel lymph-node biopsy at primary thickness of at least 0.8 mm; the decision depends on staging context and informed discussion.
Sentinel-node biopsy is never used in melanoma.
Mohs margin clearance replaces melanoma staging.
A negative node examination eliminates the need for pathology staging.

practiceQuestions.rationale: The NCI PDQ describes considering SLNB at ≥0.8 mm in clinically node-negative patients. This is not an automatic directive; current guideline and patient details govern.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which description best characterizes the public ABD MDS examination?

options.text: An ABD subspecialty certification examination in Micrographic Dermatologic Surgery, distinct from the general dermatology certificate but not a separate board organization.
A separate independent specialty board examination administered by ACGME.
An examination administered by the American College of Mohs Surgery.
A license to perform surgery for anyone passing this self-study course.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABD identifies MDS as a subspecialty certification examination. ACGME accredits training, and the education course cannot confer certificate, licensure, or procedural authority.

practiceQuestions.stem: As of the ABD notice for the 2026 exam administration, what is the training-pathway qualifier for the MDS examination?

options.text: Dermatologists must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship; the ABD practice pathway ended with the 2025 administration.
Any physician may sit after watching a free video series.
The MDS exam was permanently discontinued.
Only completion of an MPH qualifies.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABD’s notice states the practice pathway ends with 2025 and beginning in 2026 candidates must complete an ACGME-accredited MSDO fellowship. The board alone determines individual eligibility.

practiceQuestions.stem: During a Mohs map review, a residual tumor focus is found in one mapped sector. What is the core interpretive next step?

options.text: Correlate the slide focus with specimen orientation and the map so any further tissue is directed to the corresponding positive area under supervised procedure.
Remove the entire surrounding facial unit without remapping.
Call the entire margin clear because other sectors are negative.
Ignore orientation and close the wound immediately.

practiceQuestions.rationale: Mohs depends on orientation, color coding, slide-to-map correlation, and targeted additional stages until margins are clear. This educational explanation is not procedural authorization.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which is the most appropriate teaching response when a case involves a tumor extending toward orbit or bone, or margin control cannot be safely continued?

options.text: Recognize limits and escalate to the appropriate multidisciplinary/surgical team rather than pursuing margins at any cost.
Continue regardless of anatomy, bleeding, anesthesia, or patient safety.
Treat the AUC as a substitute for clinical judgment.
Assume all tumors are safely manageable in an outpatient Mohs setting.

practiceQuestions.rationale: ABD study guide specifically notes rare termination contexts and ACGME requires referral/ multidisciplinary decision-making; patient safety and anatomical limits prevail.

practiceQuestions.stem: DermNet shows a five-stage Mohs case with a cheek advancement flap. What is the correct reuse rule for this curriculum?

options.text: Link learners to the original DermNet page; if using a watermarked image for noncommercial teaching, follow the posted attribution, link, no-derivatives, and watermark terms.
Download all images and republish them because the page is free to view.
Remove the watermark to improve clarity.
Feed the images into an AI model because they are publicly viewable.

practiceQuestions.rationale: DermNet retains copyright/licensor rights. Its watermarked educational-use terms specify CC BY-NC-ND 4.0 conditions; public viewing does not grant unrestricted copying, modification, redistribution, or AI training.

practiceQuestions.stem: Which statement is accurate about MCC treatment framing in the NCI PDQ?

options.text: MCC management is stage-dependent and multidisciplinary; for distant metastatic disease single-agent immunotherapy is the preferred initial systemic approach in the current PDQ.
Mohs is the sole treatment for all MCC stages.
Chemotherapy is proven to yield permanent disease control for every stage IV patient.
Radiation and systemic treatment never have a role.

practiceQuestions.rationale: NCI describes localized/regional surgery and radiation options and, for stage IV, single-agent immunotherapy as preferred initial systemic therapy; decisions require current oncology review.
